articles.title: How Physical Therapists Can Prevent Future Health Problems
articles.titleZh: 物理治療師如何預防未來的健康問題

s: Many of us might only seek out physical therapists if we are recovering from accidental injuries or surgery.
我們許多人可能只有在從意外傷害或手術中復原時，才會去找物理治療師。
However, medical experts say these specialists can also help prevent many health problems if they are seen on a regular basis.
然而，醫學專家表示，如果定期就診，這些專業人員也能幫助預防許多健康問題。
One leader in the industry, Sharon Dunn, even calls physical therapists “the best-kept secret in health care.
業界領袖之一雪倫·鄧恩（Sharon Dunn）甚至稱物理治療師是「醫療保健界保守得最好的祕密」。
Dunn is the past president of the American Physical Therapy Association (APTA).
鄧恩是美國物理治療協會（APTA）前任會長。
She recently told The Associated Press she thinks people need to look at physical therapists in a new way – as health practitioners who can help identify possible medical issues before they appear.
她最近告訴美聯社，她認為人們需要用新的方式看待物理治療師——把他們視為能在醫療問題出現之前，就協助找出潛在問題的醫療從業人員。
Other health experts share this opinion.
其他健康專家也抱持相同看法。
They include Roger Herr, the current president of the APTA, and Gammon Earhart of Washington University in St. Louis.
其中包括美國物理治療協會現任會長羅傑·赫爾（Roger Herr），以及聖路易華盛頓大學的蓋蒙·厄哈特（Gammon Earhart）。
They both shared Dunn’s prevention message in separate discussions with the AP.
兩人在與美聯社的個別訪談中，都表達了與鄧恩相同的預防觀念。

paras.h: Follow the example of dental care

s: Earhart urges people to think about physical therapists just as they do dentists.
厄哈特呼籲人們像看待牙醫一樣看待物理治療師。
“Even if you’re not having any problem, you go in and have everything checked out.
「即使你沒有任何問題，你也會去把所有地方都檢查一遍。」
She noted that such examinations could help find and deal with problems early.
她指出，這類檢查有助於及早發現並處理問題。
For example, an exam could include a patient’s health history and current health – things like physical activity, sleep, nutrition, and so on.
例如，檢查內容可能包括病人的病史和目前的健康狀況——像是身體活動、睡眠、營養等等。
This could be followed by a look at how a person is moving.
接著可能會觀察一個人的動作方式。
Exams might uncover things like postural issues or unusual body movements.
檢查可能會發現姿勢問題或不尋常的身體動作等狀況。
Herr is a big supporter of yearly wellness visits.
赫爾非常支持每年做一次健康檢查。
He told the AP he believes physical therapists can be helpful for all kinds of people – the young, athletes, or anyone who wants to be as “independent as possible.”
他告訴美聯社，他相信物理治療師能幫助各式各樣的人——年輕人、運動員，或任何想要盡可能「獨立自主」的人。
In the United States, you can now visit a physical therapist in all 50 states without needing permission from a doctor or surgeon.
在美國，現在50個州都可以不經醫師或外科醫師許可，直接去看物理治療師。
However, a yearly exam might not be covered by a person’s health insurance.
然而，每年一次的檢查可能不在個人健康保險的給付範圍內。
This could prevent some from seeking out care.
這可能讓一些人不去尋求照護。
Earhart estimated such a visit in areas across the U.S. Midwest might cost around $150.
厄哈特估計，在美國中西部各地，這樣一次看診可能要花大約150美元。
Herr suggested a cost of $200-$300 in more costly areas.
赫爾則表示，在消費較高的地區，費用約為200至300美元。
But both experts said that in the long run, such exams might save money and can add healthy years.
但兩位專家都說，長遠來看，這類檢查可能省下金錢，還能增加健康的歲月。
“I think if people understood more that the way they move might be setting them up for a problem down the line, they’d be much more inclined to see a physical therapist,” Earhart said.
「我認為，如果人們更了解自己的動作方式可能讓日後出問題，他們會更願意去看物理治療師。」厄哈特說。

paras.h: The hips for ballet — or not
paras.hz: 適不適合跳芭蕾的髖部

s: We are all built differently.
我們每個人的身體構造都不一樣。
So, it might be useful to examine children early to see what sports or activities might be good for them.
因此，及早為孩子做檢查，看看哪些運動或活動適合他們，可能會很有幫助。
Physical therapists can carry out such early exams.
物理治療師可以進行這類早期檢查。

Earhart said, “If we screened kids as they were choosing sports and said this sport is probably not the right kind of stress for the way you are put together, it could save a lot pain and problems down the line.
厄哈特說：「如果我們在孩子選擇運動時就為他們做篩檢，告訴他們這項運動對你的身體構造來說可能不是合適的負荷，就能省去日後許多疼痛和問題。」
She added about children, “Maybe they don’t have the hips for ballet.”
她談到孩子時還說：「也許他們的髖部就是不適合跳芭蕾。」
Distance runners could also think this way.
長跑選手也可以這樣思考。
Some are built to avoid injuries despite running many kilometers while others are not.
有些人的體格即使跑了很多公里也不容易受傷，有些人則不然。
Exams by physical therapists could help identify future problems.
物理治療師的檢查有助於找出未來可能的問題。

paras.h: Fear of falling and issues with weight

s: Another area where physical therapists can help is with fall prevention.
物理治療師能提供協助的另一個領域是預防跌倒。
Falling – and the fear of falling – can be major issues, especially for the aging population.
跌倒——以及對跌倒的恐懼——可能是重大問題，對高齡人口尤其如此。
“You want to show people they can get back up if they fall,” Herr said.
「你要讓人們知道，他們跌倒了也能自己站起來。」赫爾說。
“And once they know they can do it, it gives them confidence and it can help reduce the fear of falling."
「一旦他們知道自己做得到，就會有信心，也有助於減少對跌倒的恐懼。」
He added, “One of the risks of falling is that people don’t do anything, so you don’t move and therefore you become more out of shape...”
他還說：「跌倒的風險之一是人們因此什麼都不做，於是你不活動，身體狀況也就變得更差……」
Herr said one example could be to introduce exercises involving “floor to stand” movements.
赫爾說，其中一個例子是引進包含「從地板站起來」動作的運動。
These can help improve flexibility, strength, balance, coordination, and planning.
這些運動有助於提升柔軟度、肌力、平衡、協調性和計畫能力。
“It sounds simple getting up from a lying position on the floor to stand,” Herr said.
「從躺在地板上的姿勢站起來，聽起來很簡單。」赫爾說。
“But it’s a great exercise for all age groups.”
「但這對所有年齡層來說都是很棒的運動。」
Earhart estimated about half of physical therapy patients seek help to deal with issues related to being overweight.
厄哈特估計，大約一半的物理治療病人是為了處理與體重過重有關的問題而求助。
“The more weight somebody is carrying the higher the loads are on their joints,” she said.
「一個人身上的體重越重，關節承受的負荷就越大。」她說。
Herr said he had watched extremely overweight patients successfully lose large amounts of weight.
赫爾說，他曾看過極度肥胖的病人成功減掉大量體重。
He noted that some of these individuals are motivated for a specific reason.
他指出，其中有些人是為了某個特定原因而有動力。
But for others, it is not always that clear and easy.
但對其他人來說，事情並不總是那麼明確、那麼容易。
“I have seen people change based on a milestone, like having a kid and they really want to be a good parent,” Herr said.
「我看過有人因為人生的里程碑而改變，例如有了孩子，真心想當個好爸媽。」赫爾說。
“They want to be a fit parent, and the same thing with a grandparent.
「他們想當個身體健康的爸媽，當祖父母的也一樣。
So that motivates people to engage because of a lifestyle change.”
所以這會激勵人們投入，因為這是生活方式的改變。」

of or relating to the position or bearing of the body
an agreement in which you pay a company to cover necessary medical costs
likely to do something
to find possible medical conditions by doing a test
the feeling or belief that someone or some group is good or able to succeed at something

articles.title: How Daylight Saving Time Affects Health
articles.titleZh: 日光節約時間如何影響健康

s: Much of the United States “springs forward” on Sunday, March 9th, for daylight saving time.
美國大部分地區將在3月9日星期日「撥快時鐘」，進入日光節約時間。
Worldwide, many other countries also observe daylight saving time, starting and ending on different dates.
在全世界，也有許多其他國家實施日光節約時間，開始和結束的日期各不相同。
The time change can leave people tired and perhaps unhappy the next day.
時間調整可能讓人在隔天感到疲倦，甚至心情不好。
But it also might even harm health.
但它甚至可能損害健康。
Some studies have found an increase in heart attacks and strokes right after the March time change.
有些研究發現，在3月調整時間之後，心臟病發作和中風的案例隨即增加。
However, there are ways to ease the effects of the time change, including getting more sunshine.
不過，有一些方法可以減輕時間調整的影響，包括多曬太陽。
The light helps reset your circadian rhythm for healthful sleep.
光線有助於重設你的晝夜節律，讓睡眠更健康。

paras.h: When does daylight saving time start?
paras.hz: 日光節約時間何時開始？

s: In the U.S., daylight saving time begins Sunday at 2:00 in the morning.
在美國，日光節約時間從星期日凌晨2點開始。
The time change will reverse on November 2 when clocks “fall back” as daylight saving time ends.
日光節約時間將於11月2日結束，屆時時鐘會「撥慢」，時間調整就會反轉回來。
The state of Hawaii and most of the state of Arizona do not make the spring change.
夏威夷州和亞利桑那州大部分地區不進行春季的時間調整。
Those areas remain on standard time along with Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
這些地區和波多黎各、美屬薩摩亞、關島及美屬維京群島一樣，維持標準時間。
Some people try to prepare for the change to daylight saving time by going to bed a little earlier two or three nights ahead.
有些人會在兩三個晚上之前就稍微提早上床，試著為改成日光節約時間做準備。
But with a third of American adults already not getting the suggested seven hours of nightly sleep, catching up can be difficult.
但由於三分之一的美國成年人本來每晚就睡不到建議的七小時，要補眠可能很困難。
The brain has a kind of clock that is set by exposure to sunlight and darkness.
大腦有一種時鐘，是由接觸陽光和黑暗來設定的。
This clock, known as the circadian rhythm, is on a roughly 24-hour cycle.
這個時鐘稱為晝夜節律，週期大約是24小時。
It governs when we become sleepy and when we are more wakeful.
它掌管我們什麼時候會想睡、什麼時候比較清醒。
The rhythms change with age.
這種節律會隨年齡而改變。
This is one reason that early-to-rise young children turn into hard-to-wake teenagers.
這就是早起的幼兒會變成難以叫醒的青少年的原因之一。
Morning light resets the rhythm.
早晨的光線會重設節律。
By evening, levels of a hormone called melatonin begin to increase, leading to tiredness.
到了傍晚，一種叫做褪黑激素的荷爾蒙濃度開始上升，讓人感到疲倦。
Too much light in the evening — that extra hour from daylight saving time — delays the melatonin increase.
傍晚光線太多——也就是日光節約時間多出來的那一小時——會延緩褪黑激素的上升。
As a result, the cycle gets delayed.
結果，整個週期就延後了。
The circadian rhythm affects more than sleep.
晝夜節律影響的不只是睡眠。
It also influences heart rate, blood pressure, hormone releases and other systems.
它也會影響心跳、血壓、荷爾蒙分泌和其他身體系統。
Sleep deprivation, or lack of sleep, is linked to heart disease, weight conditions, problems with thinking and remembering, and more.
睡眠剝奪，也就是睡眠不足，與心臟病、體重問題、思考和記憶問題等有關。
Deadly car crash numbers increase the first few days after the spring time change, a study of U.S. traffic deaths says.
一項針對美國交通死亡事故的研究指出，春季時間調整後的頭幾天，致命車禍的數量會增加。
The risk of crashes is highest in the morning, it found.
研究發現，早上發生車禍的風險最高。
Researchers suggested sleep deprivation might be responsible.
研究人員認為，睡眠不足可能是原因。
The time change also has a link to the heart.
時間調整也和心臟有關。
The American Heart Association points to studies that suggest an increase in heart attacks on the Monday after daylight saving time begins, and in strokes for two days afterward.
美國心臟協會引述的研究顯示，日光節約時間開始後的星期一，心臟病發作的案例會增加，之後兩天中風案例也會增加。
Doctors already know that heart attacks, especially severe ones, are a bit more common on Mondays generally — and in the morning, when blood is more likely to clot.
醫師早就知道，心臟病發作，尤其是嚴重的發作，一般在星期一稍微比較常見——而且常發生在早上，因為這時血液比較容易凝結。
Researchers do not know why the time change would add to that Monday connection.
研究人員不知道為什麼時間調整會加重星期一的這種關聯。
But it is possible the sudden circadian change influences other issues such as high blood pressure in people already at risk.
但有可能是晝夜節律突然改變，影響了其他問題，例如本來就有風險的人的高血壓。

paras.hz: 為日光節約時間做準備

s: To prepare for daylight saving time, experts offer some advice.
為了因應日光節約時間，專家提供了一些建議。
Slowly move bedtimes about 15 or 20 minutes earlier for several nights before the time change.
在時間調整前的幾個晚上，慢慢把就寢時間提早大約15到20分鐘。
Try to rise earlier the next morning, too.
隔天早上也試著早一點起床。
Go outside for early morning sunshine the first week of daylight saving time.
在日光節約時間的第一週，到戶外曬曬清晨的陽光。
This is another way to help reset your body’s clock.
這是幫助重設身體時鐘的另一種方法。
Start daily activities, like dinner or exercise, a little earlier.
把晚餐或運動等日常活動稍微提早開始。
This may help tell your body to start getting used to the new conditions, sleep experts suggest.
睡眠專家表示，這可能有助於讓身體開始適應新的狀況。
Daytime sleeping, the drug caffeine and light from phones and other electronic devices can make an earlier bedtime even harder.
白天睡覺、咖啡因這種藥物，以及手機和其他電子裝置發出的光線，都可能讓提早就寢變得更困難。

paras.hz: 要廢除日光節約時間嗎？

s: Americans have discussed ending daylight saving time.
美國人一直在討論廢除日光節約時間。
But so far, no official changes have been made.
但到目前為止，還沒有任何官方的改變。
Health groups such as the American Medical Association and American Academy of Sleep Medicine believe it is time to end time changes.
美國醫學會和美國睡眠醫學會等醫療團體認為，是時候停止調整時間了。
The groups suggest that staying with standard time year-round works better for human biology and sleep needs.
這些團體認為，全年維持標準時間更符合人體生理和睡眠需求。

articles.title: Rise in ADHD Cases Raises Questions
articles.titleZh: ADHD病例增加引發疑問

s: Allison Burk’s daughter was struggling.
艾莉森·伯克（Allison Burk）的女兒過得很辛苦。
The American teenager had uncontrolled emotions, a decreased ability to pay attention and trouble completing work on time.
這名美國青少女情緒失控、專注力下降，而且很難準時完成作業。
A family doctor suggested testing for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, or ADHD.
一位家庭醫師建議她接受注意力不足過動症（ADHD）的檢測。
This led to an unexpected discovery: The teen had ADHD, and her mother, Allison Burk, did too.
這帶來了意想不到的發現：這名青少女患有ADHD，她的母親艾莉森·伯克也是。
During her daughter’s testing, Burk thought, “Wait a minute.
在女兒接受檢測時，伯克心想：「等一下。
This sounds familiar.”
這聽起來很熟悉。」
“I was able to piece together that this might be something I was experiencing,” said Burk, who lives in Columbus, Ohio.
「我把線索拼湊起來，發現這可能也是我正在經歷的事。」住在俄亥俄州哥倫布市的伯克說。
She sought testing for herself and was diagnosed with ADHD — at 42 years old.
她為自己尋求檢測，並在42歲時被診斷出ADHD。
More adults are being diagnosed with ADHD.
越來越多成年人被診斷出ADHD。
Diagnoses have been rising for at least 20 years but seem to have increased sharply in the last few years.
診斷人數至少已經上升了20年，但在過去幾年似乎急遽增加。
A recent government study suggested that more than 15 million adults in the United States — about 1 in 17 — have been diagnosed with ADHD.
最近一項政府研究指出，美國有超過1,500萬名成年人——大約每17人就有1人——被診斷出ADHD。
The condition starts in childhood, but about half of adults with ADHD are diagnosed when they are 18 or older.
這種病症從童年就開始，但大約一半的成人ADHD患者是在18歲以後才被診斷出來。
Some doctors say the number of people seeking ADHD testing is sharply increasing.
一些醫師表示，尋求ADHD檢測的人數正急遽增加。
“Just in our clinic, requests for assessments have doubled in the last two years,” said Justin Barterian.
「光是我們診所，評估的申請在過去兩年就增加了一倍。」賈斯汀·巴特里安（Justin Barterian）說。
He is a psychologist based at Ohio State University.
他是俄亥俄州立大學的心理學家。
ADHD makes it hard for people to pay attention and control their behaviors.
ADHD讓人很難集中注意力、控制自己的行為。
The disorder can be genetic.
這種疾患可能會遺傳。
Doctors often treat the disorder with drugs, behavioral therapy, or both.
醫師通常以藥物、行為治療或兩者並用來治療。
Judy Sandler is 62 years old and lives in the U.S. state of Maine.
茱蒂·山德勒（Judy Sandler）今年62歲，住在美國緬因州。
She was diagnosed in her 50s.
她在50多歲時被診斷出來。
Sandler describes what ADHD feels like for her.
山德勒描述了ADHD給她的感覺。
“It’s like there’s an engine in you and you feel like it’s always running, and you can’t turn it off except with medication,” Sandler said.
「就像你體內有一具引擎，你覺得它一直在運轉，除了靠藥物之外，你沒辦法把它關掉。」山德勒說。
ADHD has been called the most commonly diagnosed mental health disorder in American children.
ADHD被稱為美國兒童最常被診斷出的心理健康疾患。
More than 7 million children in the U.S. have been diagnosed.
美國有超過700萬名兒童被診斷出這種疾患。
The disorder was once thought to be something that resolved as children became adults.
過去人們認為，這種疾患會隨著孩子長大成人而自行消失。
But now, experts say they believe that many people are not diagnosed as kids and that the disorder continues into adulthood.
但現在專家表示，他們認為許多人小時候沒有被診斷出來，而且這種疾患會持續到成年。
Adults with the condition talk about having trouble focusing on immediate responsibilities and planning their time.
患有這種病症的成年人表示，他們很難專注在眼前的責任上，也很難規劃時間。
Some say the disorder has led to problems in their personal relationships.
有些人說，這種疾患導致他們的人際關係出了問題。
Diagnoses have been increasing in both kids and adults.
兒童和成人的診斷人數都在增加。
The recent government report also found adult ADHD was more common than earlier estimates had suggested.
最近的政府報告也發現，成人ADHD比先前估計的更普遍。
“We haven’t had (federal) adult ADHD data in a long time,” said Angelika Claussen.
「我們已經很久沒有（聯邦層級的）成人ADHD數據了。」安潔莉卡·克勞森（Angelika Claussen）說。
The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention researcher was one of the study’s writers.
這位美國疾病管制與預防中心的研究人員是該研究的作者之一。
There were signs of the rise, she added.
她補充說，其實已經有上升的跡象。
Increasing demand for ADHD medication led to severe shortages after the COVID-19 pandemic hit in March 2020.
2020年3月新冠肺炎疫情爆發後，對ADHD藥物的需求增加，導致嚴重缺藥。
A 2023 study showed the rise in prescriptions, or doctors’ orders for such medication, was notable in adults — especially among women.
一項2023年的研究顯示，這類藥物處方（也就是醫師開立的用藥指示）的增加在成年人中相當明顯——尤其是女性。
ADHD diagnoses and medication were increasing before the pandemic.
ADHD的診斷和用藥在疫情之前就已經在增加。
This is partly because of a change in general diagnostic measures in 2013.
部分原因是2013年整體診斷標準的改變。
Those changes expanded the definition of ADHD and reduced the number of signs, or symptoms, required for diagnosis.
這些改變擴大了ADHD的定義，並減少了診斷所需的徵兆，也就是症狀的數量。
But cases really seemed to increase in 2020, when schools closed and many adults were forced to work from home.
但病例似乎在2020年真正大幅增加，當時學校停課，許多成年人被迫在家工作。
“It’s very difficult to focus when you are home and you have kids,” Claussen said.
「當你在家又有孩子時，要專注是非常困難的。」克勞森說。
She said such conditions may have worsened ADHD symptoms in people with less severe cases.
她說，這樣的情況可能讓病情較輕的人ADHD症狀惡化。

paras.h: How ADHD is diagnosed in adults

s: Experts say that it was long believed that ADHD was underdiagnosed in adults.
專家表示，長久以來人們一直認為成人ADHD診斷不足。
Now, experts debate about whether it has become over-diagnosed.
現在，專家則在爭論它是否已經變成過度診斷。
There is no blood or brain test for the disorder.
這種疾患沒有血液或大腦檢測可以診斷。
Experts say it is diagnosed when symptoms cause ongoing problems in more than one area of life, and when those symptoms began in early childhood.
專家表示，當症狀在生活中不只一個層面造成持續的問題，而且這些症狀從幼年就開始時，才會被診斷為ADHD。
Experts say the best way professionals diagnose ADHD is by getting careful histories from patients and from people who know them.
專家說，專業人員診斷ADHD最好的方法，是仔細向病人以及熟識他們的人了解過往經歷。
They also might test a patient’s memory and ability to focus.
他們也可能會測試病人的記憶力和專注力。
But getting an appointment with a mental health professional can take months.
但要掛到心理健康專業人員的門診可能要等好幾個月。
And assessments can cost thousands of dollars.
而且評估可能要花費數千美元。
Many people turn to family doctors.
許多人轉而求助家庭醫師。
People also take online diagnostic tests, some of which are linked to health companies that prescribe medications.
人們也會做線上診斷測驗，其中有些和開立藥物處方的醫療公司有關。
“There is a wide variability in this country in how people diagnose, how strict they are, and who they diagnose,” said Margaret Sibley.
「在這個國家，人們如何診斷、標準有多嚴格、診斷哪些人，差異非常大。」瑪格麗特·西布利（Margaret Sibley）說。
She is psychologist at University of Washington.
她是華盛頓大學的心理學家。
The American Professional Society of ADHD and Related Disorders is preparing a set of diagnosis and treatment guidelines for American health professionals who treat adults.
美國ADHD及相關疾患專業學會正在為治療成人的美國醫療專業人員制定一套診斷與治療指引。
Sibley is leading the work on the guidelines, which the organization expects to release later this year.
西布利正在主導這份指引的工作，該組織預計今年稍後發布。

articles.title: New Flowering Plants for Gardeners to Try
articles.titleZh: 園丁可以嘗試的新開花植物

s: If you are a gardener, you probably have some favorite plants that you grow year after year.
如果你是園丁，你可能有一些年年都會種的心愛植物。
But you might also like to try new plants sometimes.
但你偶爾也可能想試試新的植物。
Gardening expert Jessica Damiano recently reported for the Associated Press about one way to find new plants that might appeal to growers.
園藝專家潔西卡·達米亞諾（Jessica Damiano）最近為美聯社報導了一種找到可能吸引種植者的新植物的方法。

Each year, the independent, nonprofit organization All-America Selections (AAS) enlists more than 80 horticultural professionals from around the United States and Canada to serve as plant-trial judges.
每年，獨立的非營利組織「全美精選」（All-America Selections，AAS）都會從美國和加拿大各地招募80多位園藝專業人士，擔任植物試種評審。
Today, we share newly developed flowering plants meant to improve the appearance of your garden.
今天，我們要分享一些新培育的開花植物，讓你的花園更加美觀。
Celosia Flamma Pink is an upright flowering plant.
「火焰粉紅」雞冠花（Celosia Flamma Pink）是一種直立型的開花植物。
This pink variety is the latest introduction in the Flamma Celosia series.
這個粉紅色品種是「火焰」雞冠花系列的最新成員。
It is a small, easy-to-grow celosia noted for strong blooming and vibrant, long-lasting flowers.
它是一種小巧、容易種植的雞冠花，以花開得旺盛、花色鮮豔且花期持久著稱。
Judges praised its good performance even in hot and humid weather.
評審稱讚它即使在炎熱潮濕的天氣下也表現良好。
It also lasts a long time in a container after it is cut.
剪下後插在容器裡也能維持很久。
The plant is bred by Clover Seed Company.
這種植物由三葉草種子公司（Clover Seed Company）培育。
Vinca Sphere Polkadot is a flat wide-petaled flower.
「球型圓點」長春花（Vinca Sphere Polkadot）是一種花瓣寬而平展的花。
Judges called this vinca variety resilient and beautiful.
評審稱這個長春花品種既強韌又美麗。
With a naturally tightly grouped, rounded appearance, the plant blooms throughout the summer.
它天生枝葉緊密、外型渾圓，整個夏天都會開花。
It grows well in hot, dry conditions and has good disease resistance and durability against heavy rain and storms.
它在炎熱乾燥的環境中長得很好，抗病力佳，也耐得住大雨和暴風雨。
It is bred by Miyoshi & Co.
它由三好公司（Miyoshi & Co.）培育。
Zinnia Crestar Mix combines “the best” crested zinnias in one seed pack.
「冠星綜合」百日草（Zinnia Crestar Mix）在一包種子裡結合了「最好的」冠狀百日草。
The pink, orange, red, white, peach and yellow flower blends well for mass plantings and succession sowing.
粉紅、橘、紅、白、桃和黃色的花混搭得很好，適合大面積種植和接續播種。
Succession sowing means growing several plants that bloom in different seasons in your garden.
接續播種是指在花園裡種植好幾種在不同季節開花的植物。
Zinnia Crestar Mix can also provide a continuous supply of cut flowers during summer.
「冠星綜合」百日草也能在夏季持續提供切花。
The sun-loving plants also tolerated heat and humidity well in the trials.
這種喜歡陽光的植物在試種中也很耐熱、耐濕。
It is bred by Takii Europe.
它由瀧井歐洲公司（Takii Europe）培育。
Dahlia Black Forest Ruby has ruby-red flowers that show up nicely against dark-colored leaves.
「黑森林紅寶石」大理花（Dahlia Black Forest Ruby）有著寶石紅的花朵，在深色葉片襯托下格外好看。
The disease-resistant plant impressed judges with its overall durability.
這種抗病植物整體的耐受力讓評審印象深刻。
It was bred by Takii Europe B.V.
它由瀧井歐洲公司（Takii Europe B.V.）培育。
Dianthus Interspecific Capitán Magnifica is a new dianthus plant.
「隊長華麗」種間雜交石竹（Dianthus Interspecific Capitán Magnifica）是一種新的石竹植物。
It thrived through the test gardens’ summer heat.
它在試種花園的夏季高溫中依然生長茂盛。
Its pink flowers, that grow on long stems, can be used as cut flowers.
它長在長莖上的粉紅色花朵可以當作切花。
Cutting the plants back after their first bloom can result in strong new growth and better flower production.
在第一次開花後修剪植株，可以讓新枝長得更強壯，花也開得更多。
This dianthus was bred by Selecta One.
這種石竹由Selecta One公司培育。
Marigold Mango Tango is a marigold that has two-colored blooms: yellow and red.
「芒果探戈」萬壽菊（Marigold Mango Tango）是一種開雙色花的萬壽菊：黃色和紅色。
The small, strong plants provide nonstop color over an extended season.
這種植株小而強健，能在較長的季節裡不間斷地展現色彩。
The variety was honored by European judges.
這個品種獲得了歐洲評審的肯定。
It can be used for plantings in garden borders and in containers.
它可以種在花園邊緣，也可以種在容器裡。
Ernst Benary of America bred this variety.
美國恩斯特·貝納利公司（Ernst Benary of America）培育了這個品種。
Nasturtium Baby Gold, Nasturtium Baby Red, and Nasturtium Baby Yellow were also praised by European judges.
「寶貝金」金蓮花、「寶貝紅」金蓮花和「寶貝黃」金蓮花也獲得歐洲評審的讚賞。
These new, small nasturtiums produce golden-yellow, rich red and soft yellow flowers that look pleasing next to their dark-green leaves.
這些新的小型金蓮花會開出金黃色、濃紅色和淡黃色的花，與深綠色的葉子相映成趣。
The judges praised their uniformly small appearance.
評審稱讚它們一致小巧的外型。
Takii Europe BV bred these flowers.
這些花由瀧井歐洲公司（Takii Europe BV）培育。
Petunia Dekko Maxx Pink is easy to grow and grows quickly.
「德科麥克斯粉紅」矮牽牛（Petunia Dekko Maxx Pink）容易種植，而且長得很快。
These spreading, flat blooms excited the judges during summer trials.
這些向外伸展的平展花朵在夏季試種期間讓評審非常興奮。
Flowers covered the plants throughout the season and held up well against heavy rain and bad weather.
整個季節花朵都開滿植株，而且很耐得住大雨和惡劣天氣。
It was bred by Syngenta Flowers.
它由先正達花卉公司（Syngenta Flowers）培育。
Petunia Shake Raspberry F1 has been compared to “a blended raspberry milkshake swirled with lemon-lime green sorbet on a superior-performing petunia.
「搖搖覆盆子F1」矮牽牛（Petunia Shake Raspberry F1）被比喻為「在一株表現卓越的矮牽牛上，混合了覆盆子奶昔並漩入檸檬萊姆綠雪酪」。
This flower resisted heat and provided colorful blooms all season.
這種花耐熱，整個季節都開出繽紛的花朵。
It was bred by Hem Genetics BV.
它由漢姆遺傳公司（Hem Genetics BV）培育。
Snapdragon DoubleShot Yellow Red Heart F1 smells like sweet candy.
「雙響黃紅心F1」金魚草（Snapdragon DoubleShot Yellow Red Heart F1）聞起來像甜甜的糖果。
It bloomed earlier than similar varieties in the trials.
在試種中，它比類似品種更早開花。
Trial judges noted its healthy, strong growth, long-lasting flowers, and good heat tolerance.
試種評審注意到它生長健康強壯、花期持久，而且很耐熱。
Hem Genetics also bred this variety.
這個品種也是由漢姆遺傳公司培育。
And finally, Zinnia Zydeco Fire is a disease-resistant zinnia variety that is fiery orange colored with strong stems.
最後，「柴迪科火焰」百日草（Zinnia Zydeco Fire）是一種抗病的百日草品種，花色是火熱的橘色，莖也很強壯。
Judges found its flowers to be larger and more resilient than those of similar plants.
評審發現它的花比類似植物更大、更強韌。
Syngenta Flowers bred this variety as well.
這個品種同樣由先正達花卉公司培育。
We hope this list provides you with ideas for your garden planting wherever you are.
希望這份清單能為身在各地的你，提供一些花園種植的點子。

articles.title: How to Reduce Risks of Bad Air Quality
articles.titleZh: 如何降低空氣品質不佳的風險

s: Air quality differs from place to place and day to day.
空氣品質因地而異，每天也都不同。
But about 99 percent of the world’s population breathes air at some point that does not meet pollution guidelines set by the World Health Organization (WHO).
但全世界約有99%的人口，在某些時候呼吸到的空氣未達世界衛生組織（WHO）訂定的污染標準。
Different forms of air pollution kill about 7 million people each year, the U.N. health agency estimates.
據這個聯合國衛生機構估計，各種形式的空氣污染每年造成約700萬人死亡。
But health experts say there are some actions individuals can take to protect themselves, even in the world’s most polluted cities.
但健康專家表示，即使在全世界污染最嚴重的城市，個人也能採取一些行動來保護自己。
The first step is to start with the understanding that air is not only polluted when it looks smoky or smoggy, said Tanushree Ganguly.
塔努什里·甘古利（Tanushree Ganguly）說，第一步是要先了解，空氣並不是只有在看起來煙霧瀰漫時才受到污染。
She is an air quality expert with the Energy Policy Institute of Chicago’s India program.
她是芝加哥能源政策研究所印度計畫的空氣品質專家。
“Blue skies can’t guarantee you clean air,” Ganguly told The Associated Press.
「藍天不能保證你呼吸的是乾淨空氣。」甘古利告訴美聯社。
Air pollutants often come from people burning things.
空氣污染物通常來自人類燃燒東西。
Examples include fuels as well as clearing operations involving crops or trees.
例子包括燃料，以及涉及農作物或樹木的清除作業。
Pollutants can also be released from wildfires.
污染物也可能由野火釋放出來。
Among the most dangerous particles we can breathe in are called particulate matter.
我們吸入的最危險的微粒之一，稱為懸浮微粒。
The smallest of these are known as PM 2.5.
其中最小的稱為PM2.5。
This is because they are less than 2.5 microns in diameter.
這是因為它們的直徑小於2.5微米。
These particles can travel deep inside human lungs and are mostly created by burning fuels.
這些微粒能深入人體肺部，而且大多是燃燒燃料所產生的。
Larger particles, known as PM 10, are linked to agriculture, roadways, mining or wind-blown dust.
較大的微粒稱為PM10，與農業、道路、採礦或風吹揚塵有關。
Other dangerous pollutants include gases like nitrogen dioxide or sulfur dioxide, which are also produced from burning fuels.
其他危險的污染物包括二氧化氮或二氧化硫等氣體，它們也是燃燒燃料所產生的。
This information comes from Anumita Roychowdhury, an air pollution expert at the Center for Science and Environment in New Delhi.
這些資訊來自新德里科學與環境中心的空氣污染專家阿努米塔·羅伊喬杜里（Anumita Roychowdhury）。
The American-based Health Effects Institute says air pollution is the second-largest risk factor for early death worldwide, behind high blood pressure.
美國的健康影響研究所表示，空氣污染是全球早逝的第二大風險因素，僅次於高血壓。
Short-term exposure can cause asthma attacks and increase the risk of heart attacks and stroke, especially in older people and those with existing medical problems.
短期暴露可能引發氣喘發作，並增加心臟病發作和中風的風險，尤其是對老年人和本身已有疾病的人。
Long-term exposure can cause serious heart and lung problems that can lead to death.
長期暴露則可能造成嚴重的心臟和肺部問題，甚至導致死亡。
A recent study by the U.N. children’s agency UNICEF found that more than 500 million children in East Asia and Pacific countries breathe unhealthy air.
聯合國兒童基金會（UNICEF）最近一項研究發現，東亞和太平洋國家有超過5億名兒童呼吸著不健康的空氣。
The pollution is linked to the deaths of 100 children under age 5 every day.
這種污染與每天100名5歲以下兒童的死亡有關。
June Kunugi, UNICEF’s Regional Director for East Asia, said the polluted air limits growth, harms lungs and affects thinking abilities.
聯合國兒童基金會東亞區域主任國際淳子（June Kunugi）說，污染的空氣會限制成長、傷害肺部，並影響思考能力。
“Every breath matters, but for too many children every breath can bring harm,” she said.
「每一口呼吸都很重要，但對太多孩子來說，每一口呼吸都可能帶來傷害。」她說。

paras.h: How to tell if air is safe?
paras.hz: 如何判斷空氣是否安全？

s: Over 6,000 cities in 117 countries now record and follow air quality levels.
現在117個國家有超過6,000座城市記錄並追蹤空氣品質指數。
Many mobile apps include air quality information as well.
許多手機應用程式也提供空氣品質資訊。
But it can be difficult to know how bad the air is by looking at these numbers.
但光看這些數字，可能很難知道空氣到底有多糟。
To help people better understand air quality levels, many countries have established an air quality index, or AQI.
為了幫助人們更了解空氣品質程度，許多國家建立了空氣品質指標，簡稱AQI。
Larger numbers on this index mean worse air.
這個指標的數字越大，代表空氣越差。
Different countries have different air quality standards.
不同國家有不同的空氣品質標準。
For example, India’s daily PM 2.5 limit is more than 1.5 times higher than in Thailand and 4 times higher than WHO standards.
例如，印度的PM2.5每日上限比泰國高出1.5倍以上，比世界衛生組織的標準高出4倍。
For individuals, experts say the goal should be to limit exposure when air quality is bad, by staying indoors or wearing a mask.
專家表示，就個人而言，目標應該是在空氣品質不佳時待在室內或戴口罩，以減少暴露。
This is not always possible, though.
不過，這並不一定做得到。
Danny Djarum is with the World Resources Institute.
丹尼·賈魯姆（Danny Djarum）任職於世界資源研究所。
He told the AP there are many people who live or work outside and “can’t really afford” to stay indoors.
他告訴美聯社，有許多人住在戶外或在戶外工作，「實在負擔不起」待在室內。
People also need to watch indoor air pollution that can be caused by common household activities like cooking or burning incense.
人們也需要留意室內空氣污染，煮飯或燒香等常見的居家活動都可能造成這種污染。

paras.h: What are the benefits — and limitations — of air purifiers?
paras.hz: 空氣清淨機的好處與侷限

s: While air purifiers can help reduce indoor air pollution, experts say they do have limitations.
雖然空氣清淨機有助於減少室內空氣污染，但專家表示，它們確實有侷限性。
The devices work by pulling air from a room and then pushing it through a filter that traps pollutants.
這種裝置的運作方式是把房間裡的空氣吸進去，再推送通過能攔截污染物的濾網。
The filtered air is then sent back into the room.
過濾後的空氣再送回房間裡。
Air purifiers work best when used in small spaces and when people are nearby.
空氣清淨機在小空間裡、而且有人在附近時效果最好。
This is because they can only clean a certain amount of air, said Rajasekhar Balasubramanian of the National University of Singapore.
新加坡國立大學的拉賈塞卡·巴拉蘇布拉馬尼安（Rajasekhar Balasubramanian）說，這是因為它們只能淨化一定量的空氣。
He added, “If we have a tiny air purifier in a large room, it won’t be effective.”
他還說：「如果我們在大房間裡放一台小小的空氣清淨機，就不會有效果。」

articles.title: New Fruits and Vegetables for Gardeners to Try
articles.titleZh: 園丁可以嘗試的新蔬果

s: If you are a gardener, you probably have some favorite plants that you grow year after year.
如果你是園丁，你可能有一些年年都會種的心愛植物。
But you might also like to try new plants sometimes.
但你偶爾也可能想試試新的植物。
Gardening expert Jessica Damiano recently reported for the Associated Press about one way to find new plants that might appeal to growers.
園藝專家潔西卡·達米亞諾（Jessica Damiano）最近為美聯社報導了一種找到可能吸引種植者的新植物的方法。

Each year, the independent, nonprofit organization All-America Selections (AAS) enlists more than 80 horticultural professionals from around the United States and Canada to serve as plant-trial judges.
每年，獨立的非營利組織「全美精選」（All-America Selections，AAS）都會從美國和加拿大各地招募80多位園藝專業人士，擔任植物試種評審。
Their job is to grow the new plants side-by-side with currently available varieties.
他們的工作是把新植物和目前市面上的品種並排種植。
The group then compares plant performance, time to reach full growth, flower or fruit size, disease resistance and other qualities important to home gardeners.
接著，這個團體會比較植物的表現、長到成熟所需的時間、花朵或果實的大小、抗病力，以及其他對家庭園丁來說很重要的特性。
When the results are gathered, the best plants are named AAS winners for the following year in time for their launch on the market.
彙整結果後，最好的植物會被選為隔年的AAS得獎品種，正好趕上它們在市場上推出的時機。
For 2025, 20 plants have been named national or local winners.
2025年共有20種植物被選為全國或地區得獎品種。
Seven of them are edible plants, meaning they can be eaten.
其中七種是可食用植物，也就是可以吃的。
Here are the new kinds of edible plants that some gardeners might be interested in.
以下是一些園丁可能會有興趣的新品種可食用植物。
Two of the winners received the honor under the regional, or local, identification.
其中兩個得獎品種是以區域，也就是地區類別獲得這項殊榮。
The Basil Piedmont of the Great Lakes and Heartland regions was noted for its strong resistance to disease, especially that of the fungus called downy mildew.
五大湖區和中部地區的「皮埃蒙特」羅勒（Basil Piedmont）因為抗病力強而受到矚目，尤其是對一種叫做露菌病的真菌病害。
The experts also favored its strong smell, classic flavor and “refined habit.
專家們也很喜歡它濃郁的香氣、經典的風味和「精緻的株型」。
Harvested plants keep for a long period, the judges said.
評審說，採收下來的植株可以保存很久。
The dense, bushy plant also was honored for strong growth and health, even in difficult growing conditions.
這種茂密、叢生的植物即使在艱困的生長條件下也長得強壯健康，因此也獲得表揚。
Garden Genetics and Seeds by Design produced the new plant.
這種新植物由Garden Genetics公司和Seeds by Design公司培育出來。
Tomato Tonatico F1 of the Mountain/Southwest and Northeast regions also was a winner.
山區／西南部和東北部地區的「托納蒂科F1」番茄（Tomato Tonatico F1）也是得獎品種。
Judges praised the taste, texture, yield, disease resistance and reduced fruit cracking and splitting of this cherry tomato.
評審稱讚這種小番茄的口感、質地、產量、抗病力，以及果實較少龜裂和裂開。
Tonatico also was noted for its strongly attached, uniform fruit clusters that were easy to remove at harvest time.
托納蒂科也因為果串連結牢固、大小一致，採收時很容易摘取而受到注意。
The fruit was created, or bred, by Bejo USA.
這種果實是由美國貝喬公司（Bejo USA）研發，也就是培育出來的。
The Cauliflower Murasaki Fioretto 70 F1 is among the five winners in the national class.
「紫色小花70 F1」花椰菜（Cauliflower Murasaki Fioretto 70 F1）是全國類別的五個得獎品種之一。
Murasaki translates to “purple” in Japanese.
Murasaki在日文裡的意思是「紫色」。
This cauliflower has bright purple flowers, as well as long, soft stems.
這種花椰菜有鮮紫色的花球，以及長而柔軟的莖。
The experts said the plant matures, or reaches full growth, early and is easy to harvest.
專家說，這種植物成熟得早，也就是很早就長成，而且容易採收。
It does not have a strong flavor and would make a beautiful purple food to serve raw, or uncooked.
它的味道不重，很適合做成美麗的紫色料理生吃，也就是不經烹煮。
It will turn to a fuchsia color in vinegar and golden brown when lightly cooked.
它泡在醋裡會變成桃紅色，稍微煮過則會變成金褐色。
Tokita Seed America bred the plant.
美國時田種苗公司（Tokita Seed America）培育了這種植物。
Winner Kohlrabi Konstance F1 is also a purple plant.
得獎品種「康斯坦斯F1」大頭菜（Kohlrabi Konstance F1）也是紫色的植物。
Judges said it grew well in both spring and fall.
評審說它在春季和秋季都長得很好。
It produced crack-resistant, long-lasting bulbs with smooth, bright skin.
它結出的球莖不易裂開、耐保存，表皮光滑亮麗。
It also offers a longer harvest period than other varieties and tasty leaves.
它的採收期也比其他品種更長，葉子也很美味。
Bejo Seeds is the breeder.
貝喬種子公司（Bejo Seeds）是培育者。
The winning Pepper Pick-N-Pop Yellow F1 was noted for “outstanding” resistance to bacterial leaf spot disease.
得獎的「隨摘隨吃黃F1」甜椒（Pepper Pick-N-Pop Yellow F1）以對細菌性葉斑病「出色」的抵抗力著稱。
Judges also found that the plant produced sweet, yellow, small peppers throughout the growing season.
評審也發現，這種植物在整個生長季都能結出甜甜的黃色小甜椒。
The company Seminis Home Garden was the breeder.
培育者是Seminis家庭園藝公司。
Squash Green Lightning F1 was praised for its small seed cavity.
「綠色閃電F1」南瓜（Squash Green Lightning F1）因為種子腔小而受到稱讚。
This results in more edible flesh from each fruit.
這讓每顆果實都有更多可食用的果肉。
Green Lightning lived up to its name in the trials, judges said.
評審說，「綠色閃電」在試種中果然名副其實。
They noted how quickly it reached maturity.
他們注意到它很快就長到成熟。
One judge said, “This entry not only looked better but also tasted better than the comparison,” adding it looked good enough to use as a decoration.
一位評審說：「這個參賽品種不但比對照組好看，也更好吃。」還說它好看到可以拿來當裝飾品。
The judge said the squash’s flavor when cooked “stood up to added seasonings.
這位評審說，這種南瓜煮過後的風味「壓得住額外添加的調味料」。
Green Lightning was bred by Joseph Stern and marketed by PanAmerican Seed.
「綠色閃電」由約瑟夫·史騰（Joseph Stern）培育，並由泛美種子公司（PanAmerican Seed）行銷。
Another winner, Squash Thriller F1, was noted for its unusual color-changing quality.
另一個得獎品種「驚悚F1」南瓜（Squash Thriller F1）以不尋常的變色特性受到矚目。
Judges also said it was easy to grow.
評審也說它很容易種植。
The plants produce 1-to-2-pound fruits with bright orange-, green- and white-ridged lines that change color as they mature.
這種植物會結出1到2磅重的果實，表面有鮮橘、綠和白色的稜紋，會隨著成熟而變色。
Sakata America bred the Squash Thriller.
坂田美國公司（Sakata America）培育了「驚悚」南瓜。

articles.title: Experts Provide Tips for Avoiding Computer-linked Vision Trouble
articles.titleZh: 專家提供避免電腦相關視力問題的訣竅

s: Computer, or digital, screens are common at work, homes, schools, and stores.
電腦，也就是數位螢幕，在職場、家中、學校和商店裡都很常見。
An estimated 104 million Americans of working age spend more than seven hours a day in front of screens, the American Optometric Association says.
美國驗光協會表示，估計有1億400萬名工作年齡的美國人每天花超過七個小時盯著螢幕。
All that screen time can cause harm.
這麼長的螢幕時間可能會造成傷害。
Too much screen viewing can lead to dry or watery eyes, unclear vision and headaches.
看太多螢幕可能導致眼睛乾澀或流淚、視線模糊和頭痛。
It can also lead to vision conditions including myopia, or nearsightedness, especially in children.
它也可能導致近視等視力問題，尤其是在兒童身上。
Some technology workers even describe short times of dizziness or vertigo when they look at screens for too long.
有些科技業員工甚至表示，盯著螢幕太久時會短暫感到頭昏或暈眩。
However, exposure to blue light from digital screens has not been shown to cause permanent eye damage, the American Academy of Ophthalmology says.
不過，美國眼科學會表示，目前並沒有證據顯示接觸數位螢幕的藍光會對眼睛造成永久損傷。
One reason for the screen-linked vision problems lies in the eye muscles.
螢幕相關視力問題的原因之一在於眼部肌肉。
Staring closely at screens for long amounts of time can cause the muscle used for eye focus to become too tense, or tight.
長時間近距離盯著螢幕，可能讓負責眼睛對焦的肌肉變得太緊繃。
“That muscle's not supposed to stay tight all day long.
「那條肌肉本來就不應該整天緊繃。
And if it does, it's like picking up a light weight and trying to hold it over your head for hours,” American Optometric Association President Steven Reed told the Associated Press (AP).
如果一直緊繃，就好像拿起一個很輕的重物，然後試著把它舉在頭上好幾個小時。」美國驗光協會會長史蒂芬·里德（Steven Reed）告訴美聯社。
It is not hard to lift, he said, “But after a while, even though it’s not a heavy lift, your body just gets tired,” he added.
他說，那並不難舉起，「但過了一陣子，即使不是很重的東西，你的身體還是會累。」他補充道。
The vision problems can affect work, family time and rest.
視力問題可能影響工作、家庭時光和休息。
As an optometrist in Mississippi, Reed sees people who are experiencing eye pain, headaches and unclear vision linked with computer use.
身為密西西比州的驗光師，里德會看到因使用電腦而出現眼睛疼痛、頭痛和視線模糊的人。
He suggests that people with such problems get an eye examination and take regular breaks from screen viewing.
他建議有這類問題的人去做眼睛檢查，並定時讓眼睛離開螢幕休息。
Here are some more tips from eye health professionals to reduce eye strain caused by devices.
以下是眼睛保健專業人員提供的更多訣竅，可以減輕使用裝置造成的眼睛疲勞。
Take a break every 20 minutes from looking at a computer.
每看電腦20分鐘就休息一下。
During the break, focus your eyes on something that is about 20 feet away (6 meters) for 20 seconds.
休息時，把視線集中在大約20英尺（6公尺）外的東西上20秒。
This will help ease tired, tight eye muscles.
這有助於放鬆疲勞緊繃的眼部肌肉。
“Luckily, eye strain is temporary,” said Raj Maturi, an eye doctor, or ophthalmologist, at Midwest Eye Institute in Indianapolis and spokesperson for the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
「幸好，眼睛疲勞是暫時的。」印第安納波利斯中西部眼科研究所的眼科醫師、美國眼科學會發言人拉吉·馬圖里（Raj Maturi）說。
“The best way to avoid these symptoms is by taking breaks from our screens or near work activities and using lubricating eye drops, if needed,” he said.
「避免這些症狀最好的方法，是讓眼睛暫時離開螢幕或近距離作業，必要時使用潤滑眼藥水。」他說。
People normally close their eyes very briefly about 18 to 22 times per minute.
人們通常每分鐘會短暫閉眼，也就是眨眼，大約18到22次。
This helps lubricate the eye naturally.
這有助於自然潤滑眼睛。
But when looking at a screen, people might close their eyes only three to seven times per minute, the Cleveland Clinic says.
但克里夫蘭醫學中心表示，看螢幕時，人們每分鐘可能只眨眼三到七次。
That is when use of eye drops might be considered.
這時就可以考慮使用眼藥水。
Some people find that using a larger computer screen helps reduce eye tiredness, or fatigue.
有些人發現使用較大的電腦螢幕有助於減輕眼睛疲勞。
You can also increase the image size on your laptop, monitor or smartphone screen.
你也可以把筆記型電腦、螢幕或智慧型手機上的畫面放大。
Sitting an arm’s length away from your screen and looking down at it also can help reduce eye strain, the American Academy of Ophthalmology says.
美國眼科學會表示，坐在距離螢幕一隻手臂遠的地方，並且稍微往下看螢幕，也有助於減輕眼睛疲勞。
Some products for computer users, such as blue light glasses, are marketed with claims that they will reduce eye strain, improve sleep and prevent eye disease.
一些給電腦使用者的產品，例如抗藍光眼鏡，在行銷時宣稱能減輕眼睛疲勞、改善睡眠並預防眼疾。
But several studies have found the glasses are not very effective, says the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
但美國眼科學會表示，好幾項研究發現這種眼鏡的效果並不大。
The group says it is how people use digital devices that causes problems, not the blue light coming from screens.
該學會表示，造成問題的是人們使用數位裝置的方式，而不是螢幕發出的藍光。
Even after stepping away from work on larger computers, many adults find themselves using smaller digital devices for reading or watching shows.
即使離開大型電腦、結束工作之後，許多成年人還是會用較小的數位裝置閱讀或看節目。
And many children use small digital devices such as laptops, tablets, and smartphones in school.
而且許多兒童在學校也會使用筆記型電腦、平板和智慧型手機等小型數位裝置。
Ayesha Malik of the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia said that too much screen time or focusing on nearby objects can speed development of nearsightedness, especially in children.
費城兒童醫院的艾雪·馬利克（Ayesha Malik）說，螢幕時間太長或一直盯著近處的物體，可能加速近視的發展，尤其是在兒童身上。
She added that anyone watching shows should do so on a television, instead of a tablet, to help avoid eye strain.
她還說，看節目的人應該用電視看，而不是用平板，以避免眼睛疲勞。
Children should follow the 20-20-20-2 rule, she said.
她說，兒童應該遵守20-20-20-2法則。
The added “2” stands for 2 hours of play outside every day, which helps with eye development, Malik said.
馬利克說，多出來的「2」代表每天在戶外玩2個小時，這有助於眼睛發育。
“The reality is that most children are engaging with screens throughout the day at school and home.
「現實是，大多數孩子在學校和家裡整天都在使用螢幕。
It becomes difficult to track the total number of hours,” she said.
要追蹤總共用了幾個小時變得很困難。」她說。
“Aim for not more than 20 minutes during any one session.”
「目標是每次使用不要超過20分鐘。」
The blue light that digital screens release can increase a person’s alertness, experts say.
專家表示，數位螢幕發出的藍光會提高人的警覺性。
As a result, their use might make it difficult to fall asleep or sleep well.
因此，使用螢幕可能讓人難以入睡或睡不好。
To give your eyes and brain the rest they need, doctors suggest turning off screens one to two hours before going to sleep.
為了讓眼睛和大腦得到所需的休息，醫師建議在睡前一到兩個小時關掉螢幕。
You can also change the setting on digital devices to lower screen brightness.
你也可以調整數位裝置的設定，降低螢幕亮度。
If you are used to watching videos at night, try listening to an audiobook or podcast instead.
如果你習慣晚上看影片，可以試著改聽有聲書或Podcast。

articles.title: Study: Electrical Medical Device Helps Improve Muscle Strength
articles.titleZh: 研究：電子醫療裝置有助提升肌力

s: Researchers recently reported new evidence from a study of a medical device placed inside the body, a spine-stimulating implant.
研究人員最近公布了一項關於植入體內的醫療裝置——脊髓刺激植入物——的研究新證據。
Three people with a muscle-destroying disease got a little stronger after using the implant.
三名罹患肌肉萎縮疾病的人在使用這種植入物後，力氣稍微變大了。
They were able to stand and walk more easily because of electrical stimulation to their spinal cord.
由於脊髓受到電刺激，他們能更輕鬆地站立和行走。
Marco Capogrosso is an assistant professor at the University of Pittsburg, or Pitt, who led the research.
馬可·卡波格羅索（Marco Capogrosso）是匹茲堡大學（簡稱Pitt）的助理教授，他主導了這項研究。
"These people were definitely not expecting an improvement," he said.
「這些人絕對沒有預期會有改善。」他說。
Capogrosso said, "They were getting better and better," over the study that lasted one month.
卡波格羅索說，在為期一個月的研究期間，「他們越來越進步」。
The implant was able to return some muscle function, at least temporarily.
這種植入物能夠恢復部分肌肉功能，至少是暫時的。
The implant was already being tested to treat paralysis in other patients.
這種植入物原本就已在其他病人身上進行治療癱瘓的試驗。
This new evidence suggests it might also aid diseases of the nervous system like spinal muscle atrophy, or SMA.
這項新證據顯示，它可能也有助於治療神經系統疾病，例如脊髓性肌肉萎縮症（SMA）。
SMA is a genetic disease that slowly destroys motor neurons, nerve cells in the spinal cord that control muscles.
SMA是一種遺傳疾病，會慢慢破壞運動神經元，也就是脊髓中控制肌肉的神經細胞。
That leads muscles to waste away, especially in the legs, hips, and shoulders and sometimes those involved with breathing and swallowing.
這會導致肌肉萎縮，尤其是腿部、髖部和肩膀，有時還包括與呼吸和吞嚥有關的肌肉。
There is no cure.
這種病無法治癒。
A gene therapy can save the lives of very young children with a severe form of the disease, and there are some medicines to slow the disease in older patients.
基因療法可以挽救罹患重症型的幼童性命，也有一些藥物可以減緩年紀較大病人的病程。
Stimulating the spinal cord with low levels of electricity has long been used to treat chronic, or long-term, pain.
用低強度電流刺激脊髓，長久以來一直被用來治療慢性，也就是長期的疼痛。
Capogrosso's team also has tested it to help people paralyzed by strokes or spinal cord injury move their arms and legs with assistance.
卡波格羅索的團隊也曾測試用它來幫助因中風或脊髓損傷而癱瘓的人，在輔助下活動手臂和腿。
The system sends electrical signals to nerves that have stopped reacting.
這套系統會把電訊號送到已經停止反應的神經。
This has the effect of activating the muscles.
這樣就能啟動肌肉。
Capogrosso wondered if that same technology might help patients with SMA by stimulating sensory nerves to signal damaged muscle cells causing them to move.
卡波格羅索想知道，同樣的技術是否能透過刺激感覺神經，向受損的肌肉細胞發出訊號讓它們動起來，進而幫助SMA病人。
The researchers at the University of Pittsburgh published their study in Nature Medicine.
匹茲堡大學的研究人員把研究發表在《自然醫學》期刊上。
They implanted electrodes over the lower spinal cord of the three adults with SMA.
他們在三名成年SMA病人的下段脊髓上方植入電極。
Using the device did not return normal movement but with a few hours of spinal stimulation a week, all soon experienced improvements in muscle strength and function, the researchers wrote.
研究人員寫道，使用這種裝置並沒有讓病人恢復正常活動，但每週接受幾個小時的脊髓刺激後，三人很快都感受到肌力和功能的改善。
Fifty-seven-year-old Doug McCullough took part in the study.
57歲的道格·麥卡洛（Doug McCullough）參與了這項研究。
"With a progressive disease you never get any better," he said, adding, “So having any improvement is just a really surreal and very exciting benefit."
「得了漸進性疾病，你永遠不會變好。」他說，並補充：「所以只要有任何改善，都是非常不真實、非常令人興奮的好處。」
All three subjects increased how far they could walk in six minutes by the study's end.
到研究結束時，三名受試者在六分鐘內能走的距離都增加了。
Capogrosso said they could walk farther because they got less tired and “even a person this many years into the disease can improve."
卡波格羅索說，他們能走得更遠是因為比較不容易累，而且「即使是已經罹病這麼多年的人，也能有所改善」。
Researchers found the improvements did not disappear as soon as the stimulator was turned off.
研究人員發現，刺激器一關掉，改善效果並沒有馬上消失。
But they did decrease a few months after the study ended.
但在研究結束幾個月後，效果確實減弱了。
Neuroscientist Susan Harkema led similar studies of stimulation for spinal cord injuries while at the University of Louisville.
神經科學家蘇珊·哈克瑪（Susan Harkema）在路易斯維爾大學任職時，曾主導過類似的脊髓損傷刺激研究。
She warned that the new study is small and did not last very long but said it was an important test of the device.
她提醒，這項新研究規模小、持續時間也不長，但她說這是對這種裝置的一次重要測試。
She said it should be tested next with other muscle-degenerating diseases.
她說，下一步應該在其他肌肉退化性疾病上進行測試。
Capogrosso said some small but longer studies are beginning.
卡波格羅索說，一些規模小但時間較長的研究正在展開。

articles.title: Saying ‘No’ at Work Can Be Good for Your Health
articles.titleZh: 在職場上說「不」有益健康

s: From VOA Learning English, this is the Health & Lifestyle report.
這裡是美國之音學英語的《健康與生活》報導。
People might find it hard to set work limits or say “no” before taking on too many responsibilities.
人們可能很難在承擔太多責任之前設定工作界限，或是說「不」。
But experts say it is important for workers to learn to set such limits, or boundaries.
但專家表示，學會設定這樣的限制，也就是界線，對上班族來說很重要。
These limits can be important in helping workers protect their physical and mental health.
這些界限對於幫助上班族保護身心健康可能很重要。
And as with any new skill, setting boundaries gets easier with practice.
而且就像任何新技能一樣，設定界線會越練習越容易。
Justin Stewart is a 36-year-old who works as a news show production assistant.
36歲的賈斯汀·史都華（Justin Stewart）在新聞節目擔任製作助理。
He told The Associated Press that in the past, he had problems setting clear limits in his work life.
他告訴美聯社，過去他很難在工作生活中設定明確的界限。
Stewart explained that when starting his career, he held several jobs.
史都華解釋，剛開始工作時，他同時兼了好幾份工作。
In addition to his full-time position, he also rented cars at the airport and did sales at a store.
除了全職工作之外，他還在機場做租車工作，並在一家店裡當銷售員。
He said his life was so busy that he said he would sometimes sleep in his car between jobs.
他說，他的生活忙到有時會在兩份工作之間睡在車上。
After a time, he had to be hospitalized for extreme tiredness and an infection.
一段時間之後，他因極度疲勞和感染而住院。
Stewart said that over time, his busy work life finally caught up with him.
史都華說，久而久之，忙碌的工作生活終於讓他付出了代價。
“While people around me praised my hustle, I eventually paid the price.
「雖然身邊的人都稱讚我很拚，但我最後還是付出了代價。」
He added, “The doctor looked at me and said, ‘I don’t know what lifestyle you’re living, but you’re too young to be this stressed.
他還說：「醫生看著我說：『我不知道你過的是什麼樣的生活，但你還這麼年輕，壓力不該這麼大。
You’re going to have to quit something.’”
你得放棄一些事情。』」
As a result, Stewart began trying to set boundaries.
因此，史都華開始試著設定界線。
He gave up his side jobs after deciding he could live without the extra money.
他認為自己沒有那筆額外收入也能過活，於是辭掉了兼職工作。
If people from the news show contacted him to work after-hours, he told them he was not available and suggested other people who might be able to help.
如果新聞節目的人在下班後聯絡他要他工作，他會告訴他們自己沒空，並推薦其他可能幫得上忙的人。
However, experts say making such changes can be difficult.
不過，專家表示，要做出這樣的改變可能很困難。
Many people already have a hard time turning down work requests –from both co-workers and managers.
許多人本來就很難拒絕來自同事和主管的工作要求。
For example, it might make some people feel good to be needed or to please others.
例如，被需要或討好別人可能會讓有些人感覺很好。
But as with any new skill, setting boundaries can get easier over time.
但就像任何新技能一樣，設定界線會隨著時間變得更容易。
Here are some suggestions from employment experts and workers for effectively setting meaningful work limits.
以下是就業專家和上班族提供的一些建議，教你有效設定有意義的工作界限。
If your goal is to do less, adding things to your daily plans may seem like a bad idea.
如果你的目標是少做一點，那麼在每日計畫裡再加東西似乎不是個好主意。
But it can actually provide more control over your time.
但這其實能讓你更能掌控自己的時間。
Bobby Dutton is the founder of event production company GBM6.
巴比·達頓（Bobby Dutton）是活動製作公司GBM6的創辦人。
Every Monday at 2 p.m., he plans the task he is most likely to delay finishing.
每週一下午2點，他會規劃自己最可能拖延完成的任務。
And to keep from becoming too busy, he even sets his daily activities, like walking his dog and eating lunch.
為了避免變得太忙，他甚至連遛狗、吃午餐等日常活動都排進行程。
If workers have a hard time saying no, they can write down what to say beforehand.
如果上班族很難說不，可以事先寫下要說的話。
And it can also help to say it out loud.
把它大聲說出來也會有幫助。
Cara Houser is a workplace engagement coach.
卡拉·豪瑟（Cara Houser）是一位職場投入度教練。
She says workers do not always have to explain themselves when turning down a request.
她說，上班族在拒絕請求時，不一定都要解釋原因。
They can simply explain they are not available, thank the person for asking, and suggest when they might be available.
他們可以簡單說明自己沒空，感謝對方詢問，並建議自己什麼時候可能有空。
Amber Krasinski grew up in a working-class environment where saying "no" to a manager could mean losing pay.
安柏·克拉辛斯基（Amber Krasinski）在勞工階級的環境中長大，在那裡，對主管說「不」可能意味著薪水會少。
As the founder of marketing company IvyHill Strategies, Krasinski worries that she will lose business if she turns down a project.
身為行銷公司IvyHill Strategies的創辦人，克拉辛斯基擔心如果拒絕一個案子，就會失去生意。
So, she often says “not yet” when one more project is too much.
所以，當再多接一個案子會負荷不了時，她常會說「還不行」。
“That phrase has helped me through a lot of situations,” she said.
「這句話幫我度過了很多狀況。」她說。
When asked for help, workers may want to agree immediately.
被請求幫忙時，上班族可能會想立刻答應。
However, when faced with a new work request, it can be better to take time before answering.
然而，面對新的工作要求時，先花點時間再回答可能比較好。
Use the time to consider such things as workload, energy level, and interest.
利用這段時間考慮工作量、精力狀態和興趣等因素。
Israa Nasir is a psychotherapist in New York.
伊絲拉·納西爾（Israa Nasir）是紐約的一位心理治療師。
She suggests that workers pay attention to the activities and interactions that leave them feeling tired or stressed.
她建議上班族留意哪些活動和互動會讓他們感到疲累或有壓力。
Those kinds of events can be put on a “No List” to be dealt with later.
這類事情可以列入「拒絕清單」，留待以後再處理。
Experts say that just because mobile devices can keep people connected to work all the time, they do not have to interfere with a person’s non-working life.
專家表示，雖然行動裝置能讓人隨時和工作保持連線，但它們不一定要干擾一個人工作以外的生活。
For example, Nasir said she found herself checking email far too often on weekends.
例如，納西爾說她發現自己週末太常查看電子郵件。
So, during weekends, she moved the Gmail app from her iPhone’s homepage to the second page.
所以在週末時，她把Gmail應用程式從iPhone的主畫面移到第二頁。
This extra step helped her avoid checking her email.
這個多出來的步驟幫助她避免去查看電子郵件。
Experts also suggest using an email signature as another tool to manage expectations.
專家也建議把電子郵件簽名檔當作管理他人期待的另一項工具。
This tool can include more than just your name and contact information.
這個工具可以包含的不只是你的名字和聯絡資訊。
You can also use it to let others know your working hours or upcoming vacation plans.
你也可以用它讓別人知道你的上班時間或即將到來的休假計畫。
And that’s the Health & Lifestyle report.
以上就是《健康與生活》報導。

articles.title: WHO Launches New Cancer Drug Plan for Children
articles.titleZh: 世衛組織推出兒童癌症用藥新計畫

s: The World Health Organization (WHO) has launched a new service, or platform, to provide free cancer medicines to thousands of children in less wealthy nations.
世界衛生組織（WHO）推出了一項新服務，也就是一個平台，為較不富裕國家的數千名兒童免費提供癌症藥物。
The WHO defines these as low- and middle-income countries.
世衛組織將這些國家定義為中低收入國家。
The first medicines were to be provided to Mongolia and Uzbekistan.
第一批藥物預計送往蒙古和烏茲別克。
The next shipments would go to Ecuador, Jordan, Nepal and Zambia, as part of the project's testing, or pilot period, the WHO said.
世衛組織表示，作為該計畫測試期，也就是試辦期的一部分，下一批貨將送往厄瓜多、約旦、尼泊爾和尚比亞。
The drug treatments are expected to reach around 5,000 children with cancer this year across at least 30 hospitals in the six countries.
這些藥物治療預計今年將惠及這六個國家至少30家醫院的約5,000名癌症兒童。
"Countries in the pilot phase will receive an uninterrupted supply of quality-assured childhood cancer medicines at no cost," the U.N. health agency said in a statement.
「參與試辦階段的國家將免費獲得不間斷供應、品質有保證的兒童癌症藥物。」這個聯合國衛生機構在聲明中表示。
The WHO said childhood cancer survival rates in low- and middle-income countries were often below 30 percent.
世衛組織說，中低收入國家的兒童癌症存活率通常低於30%。
That compares to survival rates of around 80 percent in wealthy nations.
相較之下，富裕國家的存活率約為80%。
The agency’s Director-General, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, said in a statement, "For too long, children with cancer have lacked access to life-saving medicines.
世衛組織秘書長譚德塞（Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus）在聲明中說：「長久以來，罹患癌症的兒童一直無法取得救命藥物。」
He added that the new platform aims to bring "health and hope to children around the world."
他還說，這個新平台的目標是為「全世界的兒童帶來健康與希望」。
El Salvador, Moldova, Senegal, Ghana, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are expected to join the program very soon.
薩爾瓦多、摩爾多瓦、塞內加爾、迦納、巴基斯坦和斯里蘭卡預計很快就會加入這項計畫。
The platform hopes to reach 50 countries in the next five to seven years, providing medicines for up to 120,000 children.
該平台希望在未來五到七年內擴及50個國家，為多達12萬名兒童提供藥物。
The WHO estimates about 400,000 children worldwide develop cancer every year.
世衛組織估計，全世界每年約有40萬名兒童罹患癌症。
Most of the children live in places with limited resources.
這些兒童大多生活在資源有限的地方。
The agency says about 70 percent of children in those settings die for several reasons.
世衛組織表示，在這些環境中，約70%的兒童因多種原因死亡。
These include the use of low-quality medicines, an inability to get correct treatments, or problems with the supply of treatments.
這些原因包括使用低品質藥物、無法獲得正確治療，或是治療藥物供應出問題。
The plan to establish the platform was first announced in December 2021.
建立這個平台的計畫最早在2021年12月宣布。
It is a cooperative deal between the WHO and St. Jude Children's Research Hospital in Memphis, Tennessee in the United States.
這是世衛組織與美國田納西州孟菲斯市聖裘德兒童研究醫院之間的合作協議。
The U.S. non-profit treatment and research organization provided $200 million for its launch, the WHO said.
世衛組織表示，這家美國非營利治療與研究機構為平台的啟動提供了2億美元。
The WHO called the financial commitment the largest ever made for childhood cancer medicines worldwide.
世衛組織稱這筆資金承諾是全球有史以來對兒童癌症藥物最大的一筆。
It added that the cost-free service would continue beyond the pilot phase.
它還說，這項免費服務在試辦階段結束後仍會繼續。
The platform is working on developing its sustainability – or ability to continue to provide the service - over the longer term.
該平台正致力於發展其永續性——也就是長期持續提供服務的能力。
Andre Ilbawi is with the WHO's cancer control program.
安德烈·伊爾巴維（Andre Ilbawi）任職於世衛組織的癌症控制計畫。
He told reporters the program seeks to widen the platform and bring additional partners on board.
他告訴記者，該計畫希望擴大平台規模，並吸引更多合作夥伴加入。
"This marks the beginning of a global movement to provide children with cancer the medicines that they need, regardless of where they live, or their ability to pay," Ilbawi said.
「這標誌著一場全球運動的開始，無論罹癌兒童住在哪裡、付不付得起錢，都要為他們提供所需的藥物。」伊爾巴維說。
He added that the issue of children with cancer was getting more attention in wealthier countries.
他還說，兒童癌症問題在較富裕的國家正受到更多關注。
"Childhood cancer is increasingly a leading cause of death for middle- and high-income countries…so governments are increasingly paying attention," Ilbawi said.
「兒童癌症越來越成為中高收入國家的主要死因之一……所以各國政府越來越重視。」伊爾巴維說。

articles.title: Wilbur and Orville Wright: The First Airplane
articles.titleZh: 威爾伯與奧維爾．萊特：第一架飛機

s: Wilbur and Orville Wright are the American inventors who made a small engine-powered flying machine.
威爾伯與奧維爾．萊特是美國發明家，他們打造了一架以小型引擎為動力的飛行器。
They proved that flight without the aid of gas-filled balloons was possible.
他們證明了不靠充氣氣球的輔助，飛行也是可能的。
Wilbur Wright was born in 1867 near Melville, Indiana.
威爾伯．萊特於1867年出生在印第安納州梅爾維爾附近。
His brother Orville was born four years later in Dayton, Ohio.
他的弟弟奧維爾四年後出生於俄亥俄州代頓。
As they grew up, the Wright brothers experimented with mechanical things.
萊特兄弟在成長過程中，常常拿機械類的東西做實驗。
Later, the Wright brothers began to design their own flying machine.
後來，萊特兄弟開始設計自己的飛行器。
They used ideas they had developed from earlier experiments with a toy helicopter, kites, the printing machine and bicycles.
他們運用了先前從玩具直升機、風箏、印刷機和腳踏車等實驗中發展出來的構想。
Soon, they needed a place to test their ideas about flight.
不久，他們需要一個地方來測試自己對飛行的構想。
The best place with the best wind conditions seemed to be a piece of sandy land in North Carolina along the coast of the Atlantic Ocean.
風況最好的最佳地點，似乎是北卡羅來納州大西洋沿岸的一片沙地。
It was called Kill Devil Hill, near the town of Kitty Hawk.
那裡叫做斬魔丘（Kill Devil Hill），靠近小鷹鎮。
The Wright brothers did many tests with gliders at Kitty Hawk.
萊特兄弟在小鷹鎮用滑翔機做了許多測試。
With these tests, they learned how to solve many problems.
透過這些測試，他們學會了如何解決許多問題。
By the autumn of 1903, Wilbur and Orville had designed and built an airplane powered by a gasoline engine.
到了1903年秋天，威爾伯和奧維爾已設計並製造出一架以汽油引擎為動力的飛機。
The plane had wings 12 meters across.
這架飛機的翼展有12公尺。
It weighed about 340 kilograms, including the pilot.
連同駕駛員在內，它重約340公斤。
On December 17th, 1903, they made the world's first flight in a machine that was heavier than air and powered by an engine.
1903年12月17日，他們完成了世界上第一次以比空氣重、有引擎動力的機器進行的飛行。
Orville flew the plane 36 meters.
奧維爾駕駛飛機飛了36公尺。
He was in the air for 12 seconds.
他在空中停留了12秒。
The two brothers made three more flights that day.
兄弟倆當天又飛了三次。
Four other men watched the Wright brothers' first flights.
另外有四個人觀看了萊特兄弟最初的幾次飛行。
One of the men took pictures.
其中一人拍了照片。
Few newspapers, however, noted the event.
然而，很少有報紙報導這件事。
It was almost five years before the Wright brothers became famous.
將近五年後，萊特兄弟才成名。
In 1908, Wilbur went to France.
1908年，威爾伯前往法國。
He gave demonstration flights at heights of 90 meters.
他在90公尺的高度進行飛行展示。
A French company agreed to begin making the Wright brothers' flying machine.
一家法國公司同意開始製造萊特兄弟的飛行器。
Orville made successful flights in the United States at the time Wilbur was in France.
威爾伯在法國期間，奧維爾也在美國成功完成了多次飛行。
The United States War Department agreed to buy a Wright brothers' plane.
美國陸軍部同意購買一架萊特兄弟的飛機。
Wilbur and Orville suddenly became world heroes.
威爾伯和奧維爾一夕之間成了世界英雄。
But the brothers were not seeking fame.
但兄弟倆並不追求名聲。
They returned to Dayton where they continued to improve their airplanes.
他們回到代頓，繼續改良他們的飛機。
They taught many others how to fly.
他們也教會了許多人飛行。
Wilbur Wright died of typhoid fever in 1912.
威爾伯．萊特於1912年死於傷寒。
Orville Wright continued designing and inventing until he died many years later, in 1948.
奧維爾．萊特則持續設計與發明，直到多年後的1948年去世。
Today, the Wright brothers' first airplane is in the Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Visitors to the museum can look at the Wright brothers' small plane.
如今，萊特兄弟的第一架飛機存放在華盛頓特區的航空太空博物館。參觀者可以在博物館裡看到萊特兄弟的小飛機。
Then they can walk to another area and see space vehicles and a rock collected from the moon.
接著他們可以走到另一區，看看太空載具和從月球採集回來的岩石。
The world has changed a lot since Wilbur and Orville Wright began the modern age of flight over one hundred years ago.
自從威爾伯與奧維爾．萊特在一百多年前開啟現代飛行時代以來，世界已經改變了許多。

articles.title: Methods for Protecting Earth against an Asteroid Strike
articles.titleZh: 保護地球免受小行星撞擊的方法

s: Astronomers following asteroid activity in space estimate there is a very small chance an object large enough to destroy a whole city could strike Earth in 2032.
追蹤太空中小行星動態的天文學家估計，一顆大到足以摧毀整座城市的天體，有非常小的機率會在2032年撞擊地球。
But space agency officials say even if such an asteroid keeps heading on a path toward Earth, the world is now much better-equipped to defend itself against such a threat.
但太空機構官員表示，即使這樣的小行星持續朝地球的路徑前進，世界現在也已具備好得多的能力來抵禦這類威脅。
The American space agency NASA recently estimated there was a 3.1 percent chance that asteroid 2024 YR4 would hit Earth on December 22, 2032.
美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）最近估計，小行星2024 YR4於2032年12月22日撞擊地球的機率為3.1%。
That is the highest probability predicted for such a large space rock in modern times.
這是現代對如此大型太空岩石所預測過的最高機率。
Richard Moissl is head of the European Space Agency's (ESA) planetary defense office.
理查．莫伊斯爾（Richard Moissl）是歐洲太空總署（ESA）行星防禦辦公室的主管。
While recognizing the risk the asteroid could present, he told the French news agency AFP people should not panic over such predictions.
他雖然承認這顆小行星可能帶來的風險，但他告訴法新社，民眾不應該因為這類預測而恐慌。
Astronomers have noted that the more data they gather, the odds of a direct asteroid hit are expected to keep rising over time.
天文學家指出，隨著他們蒐集的資料越多，小行星直接撞擊的機率預料會隨時間持續上升。
However, scientists say at a certain point the odds will likely drop down to zero.
不過科學家表示，到了某個時間點，機率很可能會降到零。
Moissl said he thinks it is important to remember that even in the unlikely event the probability keeps rising to 100 percent, the world is "not defenseless."
莫伊斯爾說，他認為重要的是要記得，即使在機率持續升高到100%這種不太可能的情況下，世界也「並非毫無防禦能力」。
Here are some methods currently being considered as defensive measures to keep humanity safe in case there is a real threat.
以下是目前正在考慮的一些防禦措施，以便在真正出現威脅時保護人類安全。

paras.h: Send a spacecraft to hit it

s: Only one planetary defense method has been tried against an asteroid.
目前只有一種行星防禦方法曾實際用在小行星上。
In 2022, NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) sent a spacecraft into the 160-meter-wide Dimorphos asteroid.
2022年，NASA的「雙小行星重定向測試」（DART）讓一艘太空船撞向寬160公尺的小行星迪莫弗斯（Dimorphos）。
The effort successfully changed the asteroid’s orbit around a larger space rock.
這項行動成功改變了這顆小行星繞著另一顆較大太空岩石運行的軌道。
Bruce Betts is chief scientist for the nonprofit Planetary Society.
布魯斯．貝茲（Bruce Betts）是非營利組織行星學會的首席科學家。
He told AFP that space agencies could hit the 2024 YR4 asteroid with several spacecrafts, observing how each one changed the path.
他告訴法新社，太空機構可以用好幾艘太空船撞擊小行星2024 YR4，並觀察每一次撞擊如何改變它的路徑。
The asteroid discovered in December is estimated to be 40-90 meters wide -- about half the size of Dimorphos.
這顆在12月發現的小行星估計寬40到90公尺，大約是迪莫弗斯的一半大小。
"You have to take care not to overdo it," Moissl warned.
莫伊斯爾警告：「你得小心不要做過頭。」
He said this is because if a spacecraft only partly destroys an asteroid, it could send smaller pieces of the space rock heading toward Earth.
他說，這是因為如果太空船只摧毀了小行星的一部分，可能會讓這顆太空岩石的較小碎片朝地球飛來。
A separate idea would involve sending a large spacecraft to fly alongside a threatening asteroid.
另一個構想是派一艘大型太空船，在具威脅性的小行星旁邊並行飛行。
The spacecraft would not touch the asteroid, but would use its gravitational force to pull it away from Earth.
這艘太空船不會碰觸小行星，而是利用自身的引力把它拉離地球。
Moissl said another non-contact plan would put a spacecraft near the asteroid to eject a continuous flow of atoms to push the asteroid off course.
莫伊斯爾說，另一種非接觸式計畫是把太空船放在小行星附近，持續噴射原子流，把小行星推離原本的軌道。
Scientists have also considered painting one side of the asteroid white.
科學家也考慮過把小行星的一側漆成白色。
They believe this could increase the light the object reflects to make it slowly change course.
他們認為這樣可以增加這個天體反射的光，使它慢慢改變方向。
One idea is to use a nuclear weapon against a threatening asteroid.
其中一個構想是對具威脅性的小行星使用核子武器。
In laboratory tests, researchers found that X-rays from a nuclear blast could move a rock.
研究人員在實驗室測試中發現，核爆產生的X光可以移動岩石。
But this is considered more of a plan for kilometers-wide asteroids like the one that killed off the dinosaurs.
但這被認為比較適合用來對付寬達數公里的小行星，例如造成恐龍滅絕的那一顆。
And this method also carries the risk that a nuclear explosion could send additional pieces of the asteroid falling toward Earth.
而且這種方法也有風險，核爆可能會讓更多小行星碎片朝地球墜落。
A similar method – but one considered less dangerous – would involve shooting laser beams from a spacecraft to destroy the side of an asteroid in an effort to push it away from Earth.
一種類似但被認為較不危險的方法，是從太空船發射雷射光束，破壞小行星的一側，藉此把它推離地球。
Moissl said that if all else fails, at least the world will have a good idea where a threatening asteroid would strike.
莫伊斯爾說，如果其他方法都失敗，至少世界會相當清楚具威脅性的小行星會撞擊哪裡。
Since astronomers believe most asteroids would at most threaten to destroy one city, efforts could be organized to get people out of an area before a strike.
由於天文學家認為大多數小行星頂多只會威脅到一座城市，因此可以組織行動，在撞擊之前把人們撤離該地區。
"Seven-and-a-half years is a long time to prepare," Moissl added.
莫伊斯爾補充說：「七年半是很長的準備時間。」
He also noted that even with the rising odds involving 2024 YR4, there is still about a 97 percent chance the asteroid will miss Earth.
他也指出，即使2024 YR4的撞擊機率上升，這顆小行星仍有大約97%的機會會錯過地球。

words.def: any of the small rocky celestial bodies found especially between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter
of light or sound. to move in one direction, hit a surface, and then quickly move in a different and usually opposite direction

articles.title: Total Lunar Eclipse to Turn Moon Red
articles.titleZh: 月全食將讓月亮變紅

s: A total lunar eclipse is about to make the moon appear a reddish color across the Western Hemisphere.
一場月全食即將讓整個西半球看到的月亮呈現偏紅的顏色。
The event will happen Thursday night into Friday morning.
這個天象將從星期四晚上持續到星期五早上。
The best places to see the eclipse will be in North America and South America.
觀賞這次月食的最佳地點在北美洲和南美洲。
Parts of Africa and Europe may also get brief views.
非洲和歐洲部分地區也可能短暫看到。
A lunar eclipse happens when the sun, Earth, and moon line up just right, with Earth positioned between the sun and moon.
當太陽、地球和月球恰好排成一直線，且地球位於太陽和月球之間時，就會發生月食。
This causes the Earth to create a shadow on the moon.
這會使地球在月球上投下陰影。
In a total lunar eclipse, the Earth’s shadow covers all of the moon.
在月全食時，地球的陰影會覆蓋整個月球。
Another kind of eclipse is a solar eclipse.
另一種食是日食。
In a solar eclipse, the moon gets in a position where it blocks light from the sun, causing a partial or full shadow on Earth.
日食時，月球移到遮住太陽光的位置，在地球上造成部分或完全的陰影。
A total lunar eclipse can also be called a blood moon.
月全食也可以稱為「血月」。
It makes the moon appear reddish-orange, similar to the element copper.
它會讓月亮看起來呈紅橘色，類似銅元素的顏色。
The color comes from small amounts of sunlight passing through the Earth’s atmosphere.
這個顏色來自少量穿過地球大氣層的陽光。
The American space agency NASA says lunar and solar eclipses happen between four and seven times a year.
美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）表示，月食和日食每年會發生四到七次。
The last total lunar eclipse was in 2022.
上一次月全食是在2022年。
This one will be visible for about one hour starting Friday morning at 2:26 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time (EDT).
這次月食將從星期五美東夏令時間（EDT）凌晨2點26分開始，可見時間約一小時。
The time when the Earth’s shadow covers all of the moon will be close to 3 a.m. EDT.
地球陰影完全覆蓋月球的時間將接近美東夏令時間凌晨3點。
“As long as the sky is clear, you should be able to see it,” Shannon Schmoll told the Associated Press.
香農．施莫爾（Shannon Schmoll）告訴美聯社：「只要天空晴朗，你應該就能看到。」
She is the director of Abrams Planetarium at Michigan State University.
她是密西根州立大學艾布拉姆斯天文館的館長。
No special equipment will be needed to see the reddish moon.
觀賞這個偏紅的月亮不需要任何特殊設備。
The total lunar eclipse may be harder to see in Europe and Africa because the moon will be close to setting.
在歐洲和非洲，這次月全食可能比較難看到，因為屆時月亮已接近西沉。
Michael Faison is an astronomy expert from Yale University.
麥可．費森（Michael Faison）是耶魯大學的天文學專家。
He told the AP, “This is really an eclipse for North and South America.”
他告訴美聯社：「這真的是一場屬於北美洲和南美洲的月食。」
Zoe Ortiz is a historian with the University of North Texas.
柔伊．歐提茲（Zoe Ortiz）是北德州大學的歷史學家。
She noted that different civilizations have observed lunar eclipses for thousands of years.
她指出，不同的文明觀察月食已有數千年之久。
This helped ancient people learn things about the behaviors of the sun, moon, and stars.
這幫助古代人了解太陽、月亮和星星的運行規律。
“They were looking at the night sky and they had a much brighter vision than we do today,” Ortiz said.
歐提茲說：「他們仰望夜空，而他們看到的景象比我們今天明亮得多。」
The ancient Greek thinker and writer Aristotle observed that Earths’ shadow on the moon during a lunar eclipse was always curved.
古希臘思想家暨作家亞里斯多德觀察到，月食期間地球投在月球上的陰影總是彎曲的。
This fact supported proof that the Earth is round.
這個事實佐證了地球是圓的。
The next total lunar eclipse will appear in the sky September 7, across parts of Asia, Africa, Australia and Europe.
下一次月全食將於9月7日出現在亞洲、非洲、澳洲和歐洲部分地區的天空。
Parts of the Americas will get the next chance to see one in March 2026.
美洲部分地區下一次看到月全食的機會將在2026年3月。

words.def: a dark area created by something blocking light
a line that bends around in the same way as a circle

articles.title: Study Shows How Earth’s Orbit Affects Ice Ages
articles.titleZh: 研究揭示地球軌道如何影響冰河期

s: A recent study suggests the next ice age will likely begin in about 11,000 years unless emissions change the effects of natural climate cycles.
一項最新研究指出，除非排放的氣體改變了自然氣候週期的作用，否則下一次冰河期很可能在大約1萬1000年後開始。
An ice age is a period of reduced temperatures causing ice to cover large areas of the northern and southern parts of the world.
冰河期是指氣溫降低、導致冰層覆蓋世界南北兩端大片地區的時期。
A group of scientists studied changes in the shape of the Earth’s orbit around the sun, the tilt of the Earth’s axis and the movement of the axis itself, called a wobble.
一群科學家研究了地球繞太陽運行軌道形狀的變化、地軸的傾斜，以及地軸本身的移動，也就是所謂的擺動。
These three motions are believed to happen in cycles.
這三種運動被認為是週期性發生的。
The Serbian scientist Milutin Milankovitch developed a theory about 100 years ago that these cycles affected Earth’s long-term climate.
塞爾維亞科學家米盧廷．米蘭科維奇大約在100年前提出一項理論，認為這些週期會影響地球的長期氣候。
The team noted that small changes in Earth’s orbit around the Sun caused predictable cycles of warming and cooling over a period of about 100,000 years.
研究團隊指出，地球繞太陽軌道的微小變化，造成了週期約10萬年、可預測的暖化與冷卻循環。
These findings permitted the team to determine how the three factors of tilt, wobble, and the shape of Earth's orbit might have affected the Earth’s climate over the last 900,000 years.
這些發現讓團隊得以判斷傾斜、擺動和地球軌道形狀這三項因素，在過去90萬年間可能如何影響地球的氣候。
The group published its findings in Science on February 27.
該團隊於2月27日在《科學》期刊發表了研究結果。
The scientists examined a million-year record of climate by looking at ice sheets across the northern half of the world and deep ocean temperatures.
科學家透過觀察北半球各地的冰層和深海溫度，檢視了長達百萬年的氣候紀錄。
They then compared this data with small but regular changes in Earth’s orbit over time.
接著，他們將這些資料與地球軌道隨時間發生的微小但規律的變化進行比對。
The lead writer of the study is Stephen Barker, a professor at Cardiff University in Britain.
這項研究的主要作者是英國卡地夫大學教授史蒂芬．巴克（Stephen Barker）。

He told the French News Agency (AFP) that for many years it has been difficult for scientists to show exactly how small changes in Earth’s orbit have led to huge changes between warm and cold periods.
他告訴法新社（AFP），多年來科學家一直很難確切說明，地球軌道的微小變化如何導致溫暖期與寒冷期之間的巨大變化。
Earth is believed to go through cycles of ice ages and warm periods.
一般認為地球會經歷冰河期與溫暖期的循環。
The last ice age is thought to have ended around 11,700 years ago.
上一次冰河期被認為大約在1萬1700年前結束。
Scientists, such as Milankovitch, have long seen a connection between Earth's orbit and climate.
像米蘭科維奇這樣的科學家，很早就看出地球軌道與氣候之間的關聯。
However, researchers have struggled to precisely date when each of the climate changes happened.
然而，研究人員一直難以精確判定每次氣候變化發生的時間。
It has also been difficult for them to know exactly which orbit positions affect the start and stop of cold or warm periods.
他們也很難確切知道，究竟是哪些軌道位置影響了寒冷期或溫暖期的開始與結束。
Barker said his team of researchers studied slow changes in temperature over long periods of time instead of only looking at shorter periods of change between cold and warm climates.
巴克說，他的研究團隊研究的是長時間內溫度的緩慢變化，而不是只看冷暖氣候之間較短期的變化。
Barker told AFP, "We would expect a glaciation to occur within the next 11,000 years, and it would end in 66,000 years' time."
巴克告訴法新社：「我們預期在未來1萬1000年內會發生冰川作用，並在6萬6000年後結束。」
Lorraine Lisiecki is a professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and a co-writer of the study.
羅琳．利西基（Lorraine Lisiecki）是加州大學聖塔芭芭拉分校教授，也是這項研究的共同作者。
She said the study shows that changes in climate over tens of thousands of years are not random.
她說，這項研究顯示，數萬年間的氣候變化並非隨機發生。
The team aims to expand its findings to investigate the long-term effects of human activity on climate.
該團隊的目標是擴大研究成果，探討人類活動對氣候的長期影響。
They also want to find out how it might affect Earth’s natural climate cycles.
他們也想了解人類活動可能如何影響地球的自然氣候週期。

articles.title: A Short History of Spacecraft Landings on the Moon
articles.titleZh: 太空船登陸月球簡史

s: Many years have passed since the first spacecraft landed on the moon in 1966.
自從第一艘太空船於1966年登陸月球以來，已經過了許多年。
From then until now, there have been many additional attempts with some succeeding and others failing.
從那時到現在，又有許多次登月嘗試，有些成功，有些失敗。
Here is a short history of some of these attempts.
以下是其中一些嘗試的簡短歷史。
The Soviet Union’s Luna 9 spacecraft was the first to land on the moon.
蘇聯的月球9號是第一艘登陸月球的太空船。
It touched down on the lunar surface in 1966.
它於1966年降落在月球表面。
The landing came after several other Soviet spacecraft either did not reach the moon or crashed on the surface.
在這次登陸之前，蘇聯已有好幾艘太空船不是沒抵達月球，就是墜毀在月面上。
The American space agency NASA says Luna 9 was the first spacecraft to carry out a soft landing on the moon.
美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）表示，月球9號是第一艘在月球上軟著陸的太空船。
It was also the first to send “photographic data” from the moon’s surface to Earth.
它也是第一艘從月球表面將「攝影資料」傳回地球的太空船。
Luna 9’s landing proved “the lunar surface could support the weight of a lander and that an object would not sink into a loose layer of dust as some models predicted,” NASA said.
NASA表示，月球9號的登陸證明了「月球表面能夠承受登陸器的重量，而且物體不會像某些模型所預測的那樣陷入鬆散的塵土層中」。
In May 1966, the United States followed with its Surveyor 1 mission.
1966年5月，美國接著執行了測量員1號任務。
NASA describes this effort as “the first of a series of seven robotic spacecraft sent to the moon to gather data in preparation for NASA's Apollo missions.
NASA形容這項行動是「一系列七艘機器人太空船中的第一艘，它們被送往月球蒐集資料，為NASA的阿波羅任務做準備。」
The successful soft landing of Surveyor 1 “was one of the great successes of NASA's early lunar and interplanetary program.”
測量員1號成功軟著陸，「是NASA早期月球及行星際計畫的重大成就之一。」
Both the U.S. and Soviet Union had other successful robotic landings.
美國和蘇聯後來都還有其他成功的機器人登陸任務。
Next, the countries aimed to be the first to land humans on the moon.
接下來，兩國的目標是搶先讓人類登上月球。
In 1969, NASA successfully landed Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the moon.
1969年，NASA成功讓阿波羅11號太空人尼爾．阿姆斯壯和巴茲．艾德林登上月球。
The U.S. Apollo program sent 12 astronauts to explore the moon over six missions.
美國的阿波羅計畫在六次任務中，共派出12名太空人探索月球。
Apollo 17 was the last in 1972.
阿波羅17號是1972年的最後一次任務。
The U.S. is still the only country to land humans on the moon.
美國至今仍是唯一讓人類登上月球的國家。
NASA officials say the agency’s Artemis program aims to return astronauts to the lunar surface possibly by the end of 2026.
NASA官員表示，該機構的阿提米絲計畫目標是最快在2026年底前讓太空人重返月球表面。
In 2013, China became the third country to successfully land a spacecraft on the moon.
2013年，中國成為第三個成功讓太空船登陸月球的國家。
China landed an exploring vehicle, or rover named Yutu that year.
那一年，中國讓一輛名為「玉兔」的探測車登陸月球。
China followed with the Yutu-2 rover in 2019, this time touching down on the moon’s unexplored far side.
中國接著在2019年派出玉兔二號探測車，這次降落在從未有人探索過的月球背面。
In 2020, China successfully returned samples of rock and dirt collected by the rovers.
2020年，中國成功帶回探測車採集的岩石和土壤樣本。
The mission returned about 1.7 kilograms of lunar material collected from the near side of the moon.
這項任務帶回了約1.7公斤從月球正面採集的月球物質。
Then in 2024, another mission returned rock and soil samples from the less explored far side of the moon.
接著在2024年，另一項任務從較少被探索的月球背面帶回了岩石和土壤樣本。
China has said it aims to land its astronauts on the moon by 2030.
中國表示，目標是在2030年前讓自己的太空人登上月球。
In 2023, Russia tried its first moon landing in nearly 50 years.
2023年，俄羅斯進行了近50年來的首次登月嘗試。
The Luna 25 spacecraft was attempting to land near the lunar south pole.
月球25號太空船當時試圖降落在月球南極附近。
But it is believed to have crash landed on the moon’s surface.
但據信它墜毀在月球表面。
The country’s last effort before that, Luna 24 in 1976, landed successfully and returned moon rocks to Earth.
該國在那之前的上一次嘗試是1976年的月球24號，它成功登陸並將月球岩石帶回地球。
After its first lander crashed into the moon in 2019, India made its second attempt in 2023.
印度的第一艘登陸器於2019年墜毀在月球上之後，2023年進行了第二次嘗試。
The country successfully landed its Chandrayaan-3 spacecraft on the lunar surface.
該國成功讓月船3號太空船降落在月球表面。
The mission made India the fourth nation to complete a moon landing.
這項任務使印度成為第四個完成登月的國家。
In January 2024, Japan became the fifth country to successfully land a spacecraft on the moon.
2024年1月，日本成為第五個成功讓太空船登陸月球的國家。
But the SLIM spacecraft landed upside down.
但SLIM太空船是上下顛倒著陸的。
This caused some power and communication problems, but the lander was able to operate for a short time.
這造成了一些電力和通訊問題，但登陸器仍得以短暫運作。
