articles.title: Scientists Link Gene to Human Speech
articles.titleZh: 科學家將基因與人類語言能力連結

s: A new study suggests the beginnings of human speech are linked to genetics.
一項新研究指出，人類語言的起源與遺傳有關。
The research identifies a protein – found only in people – that may have helped early humans develop spoken communication.
這項研究找出了一種只存在於人類身上的蛋白質，它可能幫助早期人類發展出口語溝通能力。
Scientists involved in the study say this new speaking ability became important for humans’ survival.
參與研究的科學家表示，這種新的說話能力對人類的生存變得很重要。
For example, speech permitted individuals to share information, organize activities and pass down knowledge.
例如，語言讓個體能夠分享資訊、組織活動並傳承知識。
These abilities are now seen as an advantage humans had over their relatives, such as the Neanderthals and Denisovans.
這些能力如今被視為人類勝過尼安德塔人和丹尼索瓦人等近親的優勢。
The researchers recently published their findings in a study in the journal Nature Communications.
研究人員最近在《自然通訊》期刊上發表了他們的研究結果。
Liza Finestack teaches about speech and hearing at the University of Minnesota.
麗莎．芬斯塔克（Liza Finestack）在明尼蘇達大學教授言語與聽力相關課程。
She told The Associated Press (AP) the new study is "a good first step to start looking at the specific genes" that may affect speech and language development.
她告訴美聯社（AP），這項新研究是「開始探究」可能影響言語和語言發展的「特定基因的良好第一步」。
Finestack was not involved in the study.
芬斯塔克並未參與這項研究。
Dr. Robert Darnell has long been studying the protein – called NOVA1 – at his laboratory at New York’s Rockefeller University.
羅伯特．達內爾（Robert Darnell）博士長期在紐約洛克斐勒大學的實驗室研究這種名為NOVA1的蛋白質。
He helped lead the new research and was a writer of the study.
他協助主導了這項新研究，也是研究報告的作者之一。
Darnell told the AP the genetic version, or variant, included the protein that helped humans develop into the “dominant species” that remains today.
達內爾告訴美聯社，這個基因版本，也就是變異型，包含了幫助人類發展成延續至今的「優勢物種」的蛋白質。
The latest research involved scientists using CRISPR gene editing methods to replace the NOVA1 protein found in mice with the one found in humans.
在最新的研究中，科學家使用CRISPR基因編輯技術，把小鼠體內的NOVA1蛋白質換成人類的版本。
The aim was to test the real-life effects of the genetic variant.
目的是測試這種基因變異型在現實中的影響。
The researchers were surprised to learn that the variant changed the way the animals called out to each other.
研究人員驚訝地發現，這種變異型改變了這些動物彼此呼叫的方式。
Baby mice with the human variant made a different sound than normal mice do when their mother came around.
帶有人類變異型的幼鼠在母鼠靠近時，發出的聲音和一般小鼠不同。
Adult male mice with the variant also made different sounds when they were near a female they wanted to mate with.
帶有該變異型的成年公鼠在接近想交配的母鼠時，也會發出不同的聲音。
Darnell said both of these situations gave the mice a reason to speak.
達內爾說，這兩種情況都讓小鼠有了「說話」的理由。
Those with the human variant "spoke differently," demonstrating the gene’s influence in speech, he added.
他補充說，帶有人類變異型的小鼠「說話方式不同」，顯示出這個基因對語言的影響。
This is not the first time a gene has been linked to speech.
這並不是第一次有基因被連結到語言能力。
In 2001, British scientists said they had discovered the first gene tied to a language and speech disorder.
2001年，英國科學家表示他們發現了第一個與語言及言語障礙有關的基因。
Researchers called this human language gene FOXP2.
研究人員將這個人類語言基因稱為FOXP2。
But even though FOXP2 was found to be linked to human language, the variant in modern humans was not found in our species alone.
不過，儘管FOXP2被發現與人類語言有關，但現代人類身上的這種變異型並非只存在於我們這個物種。
Later research found it was shared with Neanderthals.
後來的研究發現，尼安德塔人也有這種變異型。
The NOVA1 variant in modern humans, on the other hand, is found only in our species, Darnell said.
達內爾說，相較之下，現代人類身上的NOVA1變異型只存在於我們這個物種。
The presence of a gene variant is not the only thing that permits people to speak.
擁有某種基因變異型，並不是讓人能夠說話的唯一條件。
The ability also depends on physical elements in the human throat and areas of the brain that work together to help people produce speech and understand language.
這種能力也取決於人類喉嚨的生理構造，以及大腦中協同運作、幫助人們發出言語和理解語言的區域。
Darnell said he hopes the recent work can lead to new ways to treat speech-related problems.
達內爾說，他希望這項最新研究能帶來治療言語相關問題的新方法。
The University of Minnesota's Finestack noted the genetic findings could also one day permit scientists to identify people who might need help developing speech and language early in life.
明尼蘇達大學的芬斯塔克指出，這些基因研究結果未來也可能讓科學家及早找出在言語和語言發展上可能需要協助的人。
"That's certainly a possibility," she said.
她說：「那當然是有可能的。」

articles.title: Private Lander Carrying NASA Experiments Lands on the Moon
articles.titleZh: 載有NASA實驗的民間登陸器登陸月球

s: A private spacecraft carrying several science experiments has successfully landed on the moon.
一艘載有多項科學實驗的民間太空船已成功登陸月球。
The lander, called Blue Ghost, was built by the American company Firefly Aerospace.
這艘名為「藍色幽靈」的登陸器由美國螢火蟲航太公司（Firefly Aerospace）打造。
The spacecraft touched down March 2 on the part of the moon’s near side called Mare Crisium.
這艘太空船於3月2日降落在月球正面名為危海的區域。
The near side of the moon is the side facing Earth.
月球正面是面向地球的那一側。
Officials at Firefly’s Mission Control center near Austin, Texas, confirmed the successful landing.
螢火蟲公司位於德州奧斯汀附近的任務控制中心官員證實了這次成功登陸。
The chief engineer for the Blue Ghost mission, Will Coogan, announced to excited workers: “We’re on the moon.”
藍色幽靈任務的總工程師威爾．庫根（Will Coogan）向興奮的員工宣布：「我們登上月球了。」
The officials said the spacecraft landed in the right position and was operating normally.
官員表示，這艘太空船降落在正確的位置，並且運作正常。
The successful touchdown makes Firefly the first private company to land a spacecraft on the moon without crashing or having a major problem.
這次成功著陸使螢火蟲公司成為第一家讓太空船登陸月球、且沒有墜毀或發生重大問題的民間公司。
Only five countries can claim successful moon landings: Russia, the United States, China, India and Japan.
只有五個國家能宣稱成功登月：俄羅斯、美國、中國、印度和日本。
Blue Ghost is named after a rare kind of firefly found in the U.S. The four-legged lander is two meters tall and 3.5 meters wide.
「藍色幽靈」是以美國一種罕見的螢火蟲命名。這架四腳登陸器高2公尺、寬3.5公尺。
It launched in mid-January from Florida, carrying 10 experiments for the American space agency NASA.
它於1月中旬從佛羅里達州發射，為美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）載運了10項實驗。
In a statement, NASA said the 10 experiments are designed to operate on the surface of the moon for one lunar day, which is about 14 Earth days.
NASA在一份聲明中表示，這10項實驗的設計是要在月球表面運作一個月球日，大約相當於地球上的14天。
The Associated Press reported that NASA paid $101 million for the spacecraft and $44 million for the equipment it carried.
據美聯社報導，NASA為這艘太空船支付了1億100萬美元，並為它載運的設備支付了4400萬美元。
It was the third mission under NASA’s Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program.
這是NASA「商業月球酬載服務」（CLPS）計畫下的第三次任務。
The program aims to turn over the country’s major space missions to private companies to reduce costs.
該計畫的目標是把國家的重大太空任務交給民間公司執行，以降低成本。
Several other companies are part of the program.
另外還有好幾家公司參與這項計畫。
Another lander, called Athena, is set to attempt a moon landing on March 6.
另一艘名為「雅典娜」的登陸器預定於3月6日嘗試登月。
That four-meter-tall spacecraft was built and operated by Houston-based Intuitive Machines.
這艘高4公尺的太空船由總部位於休士頓的直覺機器公司（Intuitive Machines）打造和操作。
It will land on another part of the moon, about 160 kilometers from the lunar south pole.
它將降落在月球的另一個區域，距離月球南極約160公里。
A third lander from private Japanese company ispace will attempt a moon landing in about three months.
第三艘登陸器來自日本民間公司ispace，將在大約三個月後嘗試登月。
The lander, called Resilience, shared its rocket ride with Blue Ghost.
這艘名為「韌性」的登陸器與藍色幽靈搭乘同一枚火箭升空。
But it took a longer path to the moon.
但它走了一條較長的路徑前往月球。
The company is also attempting to land on the moon for the second time.
這家公司也是第二次嘗試登陸月球。
Its first lander crashed in 2023.
它的第一艘登陸器在2023年墜毀。
NASA has said it aims to have two private landers launch to the moon each year, realizing some missions will fail.
NASA表示，目標是每年讓兩艘民間登陸器發射前往月球，同時也明白有些任務會失敗。
The space agency’s top science officer is Nicky Fox.
這個太空機構的最高科學主管是妮奇．福克斯（Nicky Fox）。
She told the AP the latest launches “open up a whole new way for us to get more science to space and to the moon."
她告訴美聯社，最近的這幾次發射「為我們開啟了一種全新的方式，能把更多科學送上太空和月球。」
In the past, NASA’s successful moon landings involving astronauts cost billions of dollars.
過去，NASA載有太空人的成功登月任務花費高達數十億美元。
But Firefly chief Jason Kim said the private companies now building and launching spacecraft have a limited budget and the spacecraft operate robotically.
但螢火蟲公司執行長金傑森（Jason Kim）表示，現在打造和發射太空船的民間公司預算有限，而且太空船是以機器人方式自動運作。
Kim said everything went just as planned with Blue Ghost’s landing.
金傑森說，藍色幽靈的登陸過程一切都按照計畫進行。
“We got some moon dust on our boots," he added.
他補充說：「我們的靴子沾上了一些月球塵土。」

articles.title: New Discovery Could Explain What Gives Mars its Red Color
articles.titleZh: 新發現或可解釋火星為何呈紅色

s: Scientists say they might have identified the mineral on Mars that is responsible for making the planet appear red.
科學家表示，他們可能已經找到火星上讓這顆行星看起來呈紅色的礦物。
New data collected on Mars through several methods suggests the substance, called ferrihydrite, is likely found in dust and rock material across wide areas of the planet.
透過多種方法在火星上蒐集到的新資料顯示，這種名為水鐵礦的物質，很可能存在於這顆行星廣大區域的塵土和岩石中。
The team carrying out the research describes ferrihydrite as an “iron oxide mineral.”
進行這項研究的團隊將水鐵礦描述為一種「氧化鐵礦物」。
The mineral appears reddish in color and can form in water-rich environments.
這種礦物外觀偏紅，可以在富含水分的環境中形成。
The scientists said discovering large amounts of it on Mars adds to existing evidence that the planet might have held a large supply of liquid water in the past.
科學家表示，在火星上發現大量這種礦物，為這顆行星過去可能擁有大量液態水的既有證據又增添了一項。
The research was carried out by an international team led by America’s Brown University and the University of Bern in Switzerland.
這項研究由美國布朗大學和瑞士伯恩大學帶領的國際團隊進行。
The findings recently appeared in a study published in Nature Communications.
研究結果最近發表在《自然通訊》期刊上。
The researchers noted that scientists have long wondered about the exact substance that gives Mars – which is also known as the Red Planet – its deep red color.
研究人員指出，科學家長久以來一直想知道，究竟是什麼物質讓又被稱為「紅色星球」的火星呈現深紅色。
Past studies had suggested a mineral called hematite might be the cause.
過去的研究曾認為，原因可能是一種名為赤鐵礦的礦物。
The study is based on Martian data collected by several spacecraft.
這項研究是根據多艘太空船蒐集的火星資料。
These include the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, operated by the American space agency NASA.
其中包括美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）操作的火星偵察軌道器。
In addition, information was captured by instruments aboard the European Space Agency’s (ESA's) Mars Express and Trace Gas orbiters.
此外，歐洲太空總署（ESA）的火星快車號和微量氣體軌道器上的儀器也擷取了資訊。
Some data also came from exploring vehicles, called rovers, operating on Mars.
部分資料也來自在火星上運作的探測車。
In their examinations, the researchers also used manmade, or synthetic, material designed to look and feel similar to real Martian dust.
在檢驗過程中，研究人員也使用了人造（合成）物質，這種物質被設計得在外觀和觸感上都很像真正的火星塵土。
Adomas Valantinas currently works as a researcher at Brown University’s Department of Earth, Environment & Planetary Sciences.
阿多馬斯．瓦蘭蒂納斯（Adomas Valantinas）目前在布朗大學地球、環境與行星科學系擔任研究員。
He helped write the study.
他是這項研究的作者之一。
Valantinas noted the mystery of why Mars is red had been considered “for hundreds, if not thousands, of years.”
瓦蘭蒂納斯指出，火星為何是紅色的這個謎團，人們已經思考了「數百年，甚至數千年」。
Valantinas recognized his team was not the first to consider ferrihydrite as a possible reason for the coloring of Mars.
瓦蘭蒂納斯承認，他的團隊並不是第一個把水鐵礦視為火星顏色可能成因的團隊。
But he noted, “it has never been proven as we have now, using observational data and novel laboratory methods…”
但他指出：「從來沒有人像我們現在這樣，利用觀測資料和新穎的實驗室方法證明這一點……」
Valantinas noted the discovery of widespread ferrihydrite suggests Mars once held liquid water that would have made it possible for the planet to support some form of life.
瓦蘭蒂納斯指出，發現廣泛分布的水鐵礦，顯示火星曾經擁有液態水，而這可能讓這顆行星得以孕育某種形式的生命。
"Our study reveals that ferrihydrite formation on Mars required the presence of both oxygen…and water capable of reacting with iron,” he added.
他補充說：「我們的研究揭示，火星上水鐵礦的形成同時需要氧氣……以及能與鐵發生反應的水。」
“These conditions were very different from the dry, cold environment of Mars today."
「這些條件和今天火星乾燥、寒冷的環境非常不同。」
John Mustard is a planetary expert at Brown University and was a co-writer of the study.
約翰．馬斯塔德（John Mustard）是布朗大學的行星專家，也是這項研究的共同作者。
He called it “a door-opening opportunity” for future research.
他稱這是未來研究的「一扇敞開大門的機會」。
But he added that additional study is needed to confirm the team’s latest findings.
但他補充說，還需要更多研究才能證實團隊的最新發現。
"As exciting as the new findings are, we realize that our results can only be verified by samples from Mars, which are currently being collected by NASA's Perseverance rover,” Mustard said.
馬斯塔德說：「儘管新發現令人興奮，但我們明白，我們的結果只能透過火星樣本來驗證，而NASA的毅力號探測車目前正在採集這些樣本。」
He added, “When we get those back, we will be able to check whether our theory about ferrihydrite is correct."
他補充說：「等我們拿回這些樣本，就能檢查我們關於水鐵礦的理論是否正確。」

articles.title: Scientists Discover Stonehenge-like Circle in Denmark
articles.titleZh: 科學家在丹麥發現類似巨石陣的圓圈

s: Danish researchers have announced the discovery of a collection of wooden pieces placed in a circle that are believed to date back thousands of years ago.
丹麥研究人員宣布，他們發現了一組排成圓圈的木樁，據信可追溯到數千年前。
The team says the wood pieces and some other objects were found during building work in the northwestern Danish town of Aars.
研究團隊表示，這些木樁和其他一些物品是在丹麥西北部小鎮奧斯（Aars）的建築工程中發現的。
The discovery led the researchers to suggest the people who placed the wooden pieces might have been linked to a group who built Britain’s famous Stonehenge stone structure.
這項發現讓研究人員推測，擺放這些木樁的人可能與建造英國著名巨石陣石造結構的族群有關。
A total of 45 ancient wood pieces were discovered underground last week during building, or construction, work.
上週在建築（也就是施工）工程中，地底下共挖出45根古代木樁。
The pieces formed a circle about 30 meters across.
這些木樁圍成一個直徑約30公尺的圓圈。
In an email to the French news agency AFP, Sidsel Wahlin of the town’s Vesthimmerlands museum described the discovery as “a once in a lifetime find.”
該鎮韋斯特希默蘭博物館的西瑟爾．瓦林（Sidsel Wahlin）在給法新社的電子郵件中，形容這項發現是「一生僅有一次的發現」。
The circle "points to a strong connection with the British henge world," she added.
她補充說，這個圓圈「顯示出與英國環狀遺跡（henge）世界有很強的關聯」。
The British Museum says on its website the first stones placed at Stonehenge, in southern England, are believed to have started arriving there around 3000 BC.
大英博物館在其網站上表示，英格蘭南部巨石陣最早的石塊據信約在西元前3000年開始運抵當地。
The Danish researchers said they were also looking to see whether an inner circle might also exist where the wooden pieces were found.
丹麥研究人員表示，他們也在調查發現木樁的地方是否還有一個內圈。
Wahlin noted that in the past, other wood circles had been found on the Danish island of Bornholm in the Baltic Sea.
瓦林指出，過去在波羅的海的丹麥博恩霍姆島上也曾發現其他木圈。
But Wahlin said the circle in Aars was "the first one of this larger type that we can properly investigate.”
但瓦林說，奧斯的這個圓圈是「我們第一個能夠好好調查的這種較大型圓圈」。
Archeologists working at the building site also found an ancient settlement that included a leader’s grave and a bronze sword.
在工地工作的考古學家還發現了一處古代聚落，其中包括一座首領的墳墓和一把青銅劍。
Wahlin said her team was still carrying out detailed work in the area in an effort to estimate the age and purpose of the materials.
瓦林說，她的團隊仍在該地區進行細部工作，試圖估算這些物品的年代和用途。
In particular, the archeologists are now searching for religious-connected materials known as "ritual deposits.
考古學家目前特別在尋找與宗教相關、被稱為「儀式埋藏物」的物品。
These might include flint arrow heads and small knives or daggers.
這些物品可能包括燧石箭頭和小刀或匕首。
Wahlin said the researchers will continue looking for links between the Aars site and other groups, such as those who built Stonehenge.
瓦林說，研究人員將繼續尋找奧斯遺址與其他族群之間的關聯，例如建造巨石陣的族群。
She added the influence of other groups had already been found in some objects and graves found in Denmark.
她補充說，在丹麥發現的一些物品和墳墓中，已經看得到其他族群的影響。

articles.title: The Planets Gather for a Show in the Evening Sky
articles.titleZh: 行星齊聚夜空上演好戲

s: All seven major planets form a kind of parade in the sky at the end of February.
七大行星在2月底於天空中排成一種「遊行」隊伍。
Although two of the planets are not visible to the unaided eye, all are on the same side of the sun during the evening hours.
雖然其中兩顆行星無法用肉眼看到，但在傍晚時分，它們全都位在太陽的同一側。
This planetary grouping happens when the planets appear to line up in the night sky as seen from Earth.
當從地球看去，行星在夜空中似乎排成一列時，就會出現這種行星聚集現象。
They do not form a straight line, but they do stretch across the evening sky this year.
它們並不是排成一直線，但今年它們確實橫跨整個傍晚的天空。
The American space agency, NASA, says these astronomical gatherings are common.
美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）表示，這類天文聚集現象很常見。
A parade of four or five planets visible to the unaided eye happens every few years.
每隔幾年就會出現一次四到五顆行星可用肉眼看見的行星連珠。
A similar parade took place last June, but only two planets could be seen without the use of special equipment.
去年6月也發生過類似的行星連珠，但不使用特殊設備只能看到兩顆行星。
Six planets were visible in January.
1月時可以看到六顆行星。
Four were visible to the unaided eye.
其中四顆用肉眼就能看見。
In recent weeks, Mercury joined the group.
最近幾週，水星也加入了這個行列。
Venus, Mars and Jupiter are all easily visible in the evening.
金星、火星和木星在傍晚都很容易看到。
Saturn is now very close to the setting sun and Mercury is close to the horizon, making both hard to see.
土星現在非常接近正在西沉的太陽，水星則接近地平線，所以兩者都很難看到。
Uranus and Neptune are the most distant planets.
天王星和海王星是距離最遠的行星。
Uranus can be glimpsed with binoculars or a telescope under good conditions.
在條件良好時，可以用雙筒望遠鏡或天文望遠鏡瞥見天王星。
But Neptune is now too close to the sun to be seen.
但海王星現在離太陽太近，無法看見。
Seeing the brightest planets is easy.
要看到最亮的幾顆行星很容易。
Go outside on a clear night after sunset.
在晴朗的夜晚，日落後到戶外去。
The planets will shine brighter than the stars.
行星會比恆星更明亮。
Mars is a bright, reddish-orange light appearing high in the constellation Gemini.
火星是一個明亮的紅橘色光點，高掛在雙子座中。
Jupiter is very bright and a little lower than Mars toward the constellation Taurus.
木星非常明亮，位置比火星稍低，朝向金牛座。
Venus, in the constellation of Pisces, is the brightest natural object in the sky besides the sun and moon.
位於雙魚座的金星，是天空中除了太陽和月亮以外最亮的自然天體。
There are many stargazing apps available that can help identify the planets and bright stars.
有許多觀星應用程式可以幫助辨識行星和亮星。
The planets will slowly move lower and lower in the west throughout the spring.
整個春天，這些行星會在西方天空中逐漸越來越低。

articles.title: Knitting While Watching Movies Gains Popularity
articles.titleZh: 邊看電影邊編織蔚為風潮

s: Nearly 200 people in Vienna, Austria, gathered recently to enjoy two fun activities at the same time.
奧地利維也納近日有將近200人齊聚一堂，同時享受兩種有趣的活動。
They worked with needles and yarn.
他們拿著棒針和毛線編織。
And they watched a movie together called The Devil Wears Prada.
同時一起觀賞電影《穿著Prada的惡魔》。
"It sounds a bit like a grandmother, but it's relaxing.
「這聽起來有點像老奶奶在做的事，但很放鬆。
And…what's wrong with letting the grandmother in us express herself," joked Austrian Alexander Koch.
而且……讓我們內心的老奶奶表現一下自己，又有什麼不對呢？」奧地利人亞歷山大．柯赫（Alexander Koch）開玩笑說。
He is a 28-year-old who crochets.
他今年28歲，會用鉤針編織。
Knitting or crocheting while watching movies has gained popularity in Europe.
邊看電影邊棒針編織或鉤織，在歐洲越來越受歡迎。
Luisa Palmer was one of the organizers of the event.
路易莎．帕默（Luisa Palmer）是這項活動的主辦人之一。
Palmer said that, during the COVID-19 pandemic, "A lot of people started knitting during the lockdown alone at home.
帕默說，在新冠疫情期間，「很多人在封城時獨自在家開始學編織。
Palmer launched the knitting evenings once a month at Votiv Kino, a place to watch movies in the center of the Austrian capital.
帕默在奧地利首都市中心的電影院Votiv Kino推出每月一次的編織之夜。
"Now we need to find ourselves…" in real life, the 30-year-old told the French News Agency (AFP) before the event.
這位30歲的主辦人在活動前告訴法新社（AFP）：「現在我們需要在現實生活中找到彼此……」
People are knitting, eating, or even breastfeeding babies while watching a movie.
人們邊看電影邊編織、吃東西，甚至餵寶寶喝母奶。
This movement is the latest attempt to add different things to the movie-watching experience, said Lisa Stolze.
這股風潮是為觀影體驗增添不同元素的最新嘗試，莉莎．史托澤（Lisa Stolze）說。
She is a spokesperson for Votiv Kino, the movie house.
她是Votiv Kino電影院的發言人。
To avoid knitting mistakes, a soft light remains on during the movie.
為了避免織錯，電影放映時會保留一盞柔和的燈光。
This also helps to increase exchanges between the attendees.
這也有助於增加參加者之間的交流。
Organizers based their event on similar ones in the United States, Northern Europe, Germany and France.
主辦單位參考了美國、北歐、德國和法國的類似活動。
Since launching in December of 2024, the movie events in Vienna are usually full.
自2024年12月開辦以來，維也納的這些電影活動通常都座無虛席。
"I usually knit while watching movies or listening to podcasts at home, so movie theaters are the perfect place for this activity," said Kaja Vospernik.
「我在家通常會邊看電影或聽Podcast邊編織，所以電影院是做這件事的完美場所。」卡雅．沃斯佩尼克（Kaja Vospernik）說。
She is a 23-year-old fashion student.
她是一名23歲的服裝設計系學生。
As the movie plays, the colorful projects take shape.
隨著電影播放，五顏六色的作品逐漸成形。
The film takes a back seat, meaning it is less important than the work of knitting or crocheting.
電影退居次要，也就是說它沒有編織或鉤織來得重要。
Everyone shows off their work.
每個人都會展示自己的作品。
Experienced knitters and crocheters help beginners learn new skills.
經驗豐富的編織者會幫助初學者學習新技巧。
"You can come alone and knit in silence to relax.
「你可以一個人來，安靜地編織放鬆一下。
But if you are looking for company, this kind of event seems to me to be the right choice," said Judith Haslöwer.
但如果你想找人作伴，我覺得這類活動是正確的選擇。」茱迪絲．哈斯勒沃（Judith Haslöwer）說。
She is another organizer of the event.
她是這項活動的另一位主辦人。
People attend the events for several reasons.
人們參加這些活動的原因有好幾個。
Some say the events let them reconnect with something real that is not on a computer.
有些人說，這些活動讓他們重新接觸到電腦以外的真實事物。
Others say they can “slow down a little.”
也有人說，他們可以「放慢一點腳步」。
Palmer said, "Doing something with your ten fingers is still more rewarding…" than working at a computer all day.
帕默說：「用十根手指做點什麼，還是比……」整天對著電腦工作更有成就感。
She added that picking the right movie is also important.
她補充說，挑對電影也很重要。
Palmer likes to watch a good "cozy comedy” that she has already seen.
帕默喜歡看自己已經看過的優質「溫馨喜劇」。
She joked that it is best to avoid scary movies.
她開玩笑說，最好避開恐怖片。
They can make you jump causing you to lose your place in your knitting.
恐怖片可能會嚇得你跳起來，讓你忘了織到哪裡。

articles.title: The Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show, the ‘Super Bowl’ of Dog Shows
articles.titleZh: 西敏寺犬展：狗展界的「超級盃」

s: At America’s 149th Westminster Kennel Club dog show, Monty the giant schnauzer won the top prize.
在美國第149屆西敏寺犬展（Westminster Kennel Club）上，巨型雪納瑞蒙提（Monty）奪得最高榮譽。
The lively schnauzer beat six other finalists in New York City to become the first of his breed to win Westminster’s “best in show.
這隻活潑的雪納瑞在紐約市擊敗其他六名決賽參賽者，成為該犬種中第一個贏得西敏寺「全場總冠軍」的狗。
The prize is the most important and respected in the U.S. dog show world.
這個獎項是美國犬展界最重要、最受敬重的獎項。
While Monty came close to winning Westminster the past two years, he fell short of the big prize.
雖然蒙提過去兩年都差點贏得西敏寺犬展，但最後都與大獎擦身而過。
In December 2024, the dog won another big prize, the huge American Kennel Club championship.
2024年12月，牠贏得另一項大獎——規模龐大的美國養犬俱樂部冠軍賽。
But for dog show lovers, Westminster is considered the Super Bowl of all shows.
但對狗展愛好者來說，西敏寺犬展被視為所有狗展中的超級盃。
This year the comparison is especially fitting.
今年這個比喻特別貼切。
That is because the most respected U.S. dog competition opened on the same weekend as the Super Bowl -- the most important game in American professional football.
因為這項美國最受敬重的狗類比賽，與超級盃——美國職業美式足球最重要的比賽——在同一個週末開幕。
This rare happening came after the dates of both competitions changed in recent years.
這種罕見的情況是因為兩項比賽的日期近年都有所變動。
At Westminster, dogs first compete against other members of their breed.
在西敏寺犬展中，狗兒首先要與同犬種的其他狗競爭。
Then, the winner of each breed goes up against other dogs within different competition “groups.
接著，各犬種的冠軍要在不同的比賽「組別」中與其他狗較量。
Among the groups are sporting, working, toy, and herding.
這些組別包括獵犬組、工作犬組、玩賞犬組和畜牧犬組。
Group winners then compete in the final round.
各組冠軍再進入最後一輪決賽。
The best in show winner gets an award – a large, shiny cup called a trophy – and a place in dog-world history.
全場總冠軍會獲得一座獎盃——一個又大又亮的杯子——並在狗界歷史上留名。
The top prize, however, does not include money.
不過，這個最高獎項並沒有獎金。
In her report on the dog show, Learning English’s Caty Weaver explains that the Westminster show dates back to 1877.
在美國之音「學英語」節目有關狗展的報導中，凱蒂．韋弗（Caty Weaver）說明，西敏寺犬展的歷史可追溯至1877年。
It centers on the traditional purebred judging that leads to the best in show prize.
它以傳統的純種犬評審為核心，最後選出全場總冠軍。
But over the last few years, the organization has added agility and obedience events open to mixed-breed dogs.
不過過去幾年，主辦單位增加了開放混種犬參加的敏捷賽和服從賽。
In 2024, Sage, a miniature poodle, won best in show at the 148th Westminster Kennel Club dog show.
2024年，迷你貴賓犬賽吉（Sage）在第148屆西敏寺犬展中奪得全場總冠軍。
And in 2023, a petit basset griffon Vendéen, named Buddy Holly, won best in show at Westminster.
而在2023年，一隻名叫巴迪．霍利（Buddy Holly）的迷你貝吉格里芬凡丁犬贏得西敏寺犬展全場總冠軍。
The breed he represents is known for its rabbit-hunting abilities.
牠所代表的犬種以獵兔能力聞名。

articles.title: Mary Kay: A Leader in the Beauty Product Industry
articles.titleZh: 玫琳凱：美容產品業的領導者

s: Mary Kay Cosmetics is an international company that sells beauty products.
玫琳凱化妝品（Mary Kay Cosmetics）是一家銷售美容產品的跨國公司。
One woman started the business in the 1960s with an investment of $5,000.
1960年代，一位女性以5000美元的投資創立了這家公司。
Mary Kathlyn Wagner was born in the state of Texas in 1918.
瑪麗．凱瑟琳．華格納（Mary Kathlyn Wagner）1918年出生於德州。
For much of her childhood, she cared for her sick father while her mother worked long hours at a restaurant.
她童年大部分時間都在照顧生病的父親，而母親則在餐廳長時間工作。
Mary Kay married Ben Rogers when she was 17 years old.
玫琳凱17歲時嫁給了班．羅傑斯（Ben Rogers）。
They had three children before he left home to serve in World War Two.
在他離家參加第二次世界大戰之前，他們生了三個孩子。
When he returned, their marriage ended.
他回來後，兩人的婚姻就結束了。
Mary Kay looked for a job so she could support her children.
玫琳凱開始找工作，好養活孩子。
She began selling different kinds of products.
她開始銷售各種產品。
One night, Mary Kay was showing products at the home of Ova Heath Spoonemore. Ms. Spoonemore began giving her guests some homemade skin care products.
某天晚上，玫琳凱在歐娃．希思．史普納摩爾（Ova Heath Spoonemore）家中展示產品，史普納摩爾女士開始送給客人一些自製的保養品。
The products were developed by her father, J.W. Heath, in Arkansas.
這些產品是她父親J.W.希思在阿肯色州研發的。
Mary Kay tried the skin care products and liked them.
玫琳凱試用了這些保養品，非常喜歡。
She bought the rights to Heath’s skin care products and started her own company.
她買下希思保養品的權利，創立了自己的公司。
She paid $500 for the legal rights to the products.
她花了500美元取得這些產品的合法權利。
And in 1963, The Mary Kay Cosmetics company began operating in Dallas, Texas.
1963年，玫琳凱化妝品公司在德州達拉斯開始營運。
The idea was to sell skin care products through demonstrations in homes and offices.
當時的構想是透過在住家和辦公室示範來銷售保養品。
Independent sales representatives bought beauty products from the company and sold them at higher prices.
獨立銷售代表向公司購買美容產品，再以較高的價格賣出。
Mary Kay decided that each representative who brought other saleswomen into the company would receive part of the new person’s earnings.
玫琳凱決定，每位帶其他女性業務員進公司的代表，都能分得新人收入的一部分。
That way, experienced sales representatives would be willing to train new ones.
如此一來，資深的銷售代表就會願意訓練新人。
By 1965, the company was selling almost one million dollars in products.
到了1965年，公司的產品銷售額已將近100萬美元。
Mary Kay Cosmetics became one of the most successful direct sellers of skin care products in America.
玫琳凱化妝品成為美國最成功的保養品直銷商之一。
It continues to have sales offices and representatives in many different countries.
它至今仍在許多國家設有銷售辦事處和銷售代表。
Mary Kay aimed to grow sales based on the idea that it is best to compete against yourself.
玫琳凱以「與自己競爭最好」的理念來提升業績。
That means every individual is trying to beat their own sales records.
也就是說，每個人都努力打破自己的銷售紀錄。
Prizes for high sales marks included special paid holidays and jewelry.
高業績的獎勵包括特別招待的旅遊假期和珠寶。
Until a few years ago, a pink Cadillac was a top prize.
直到幾年前，粉紅色凱迪拉克都還是最高獎品。
After her third husband, Mel Ash, died of cancer in 1980, she wanted to help find a cure for the disease.
她的第三任丈夫梅爾．艾許（Mel Ash）在1980年死於癌症後，她希望能幫忙找到治癒這種疾病的方法。
At first, she helped organizations raise money for research.
起初，她協助各個組織為研究募款。
Later, she started the Mary Kay Ash Charitable Foundation, a nonprofit group that provides money to support research on cancers affecting women.
後來，她成立了玫琳凱艾許慈善基金會，這個非營利團體提供資金，支持針對女性癌症的研究。
In 2001, the company and foundation expanded their goals to help prevent violence against women.
2001年，公司和基金會擴大目標，致力協助防止對女性的暴力。
Mary Kay Ash also wrote three books.
玫琳凱．艾許也寫了三本書。
She worked in her business until she suffered a stroke in 1996.
她一直在自己的事業中工作，直到1996年中風為止。
She died in 2001.
她於2001年過世。
Sales representatives say Mary Kay developed a way for women to earn money and still spend time with their families.
銷售代表們說，玫琳凱為女性開創了一種既能賺錢、又能陪伴家人的方式。

articles.title: Visitors Laugh Away Troubles at the HaHaHouse Museum
articles.titleZh: 遊客在「哈哈屋」博物館笑掉煩惱

s: A new museum of laughter in Croatia is offering to help people deal with the negativity of modern life.
克羅埃西亞一座新的歡笑博物館，要幫助人們應對現代生活中的負面情緒。
Visitors to the HaHaHouse in the Croatian capital Zagreb walk into a little cloud of white smoke when they step inside.
來到克羅埃西亞首都札格瑞布「哈哈屋」（HaHaHouse）的遊客，一踏進門就會走進一小團白煙中。
Its purpose is to blow away their worries before they climb into a "giant washing machine".
它的用意是在他們爬進一台「巨型洗衣機」之前，把煩惱吹散。
Then they move down a twisting slide into a space filled with little white balls where their trip to a happier place starts.
接著，他們順著彎曲的溜滑梯滑進一個滿是白色小球的空間，從那裡展開通往快樂之地的旅程。
Forty-three-year-old Andrea Golubic is the museum’s creator.
43歲的安德莉亞．戈魯比奇（Andrea Golubic）是這座博物館的創辦人。
Golubic said she got the idea during the COVID-19 pandemic.
戈魯比奇說，她是在新冠疫情期間想到這個點子的。
At that time, many people were feeling down, depressed and alone: "I realized that I had a mission -- to heal people with laughter."
當時許多人感到低落、憂鬱又孤單：「我意識到自己有個使命——用笑聲療癒人們。」
The idea "came straight from the heart", Golubic told the French News Agency (AFP).
戈魯比奇告訴法新社（AFP），這個點子「發自內心」。
She had ideas for many of the museum elements in one day: “that's how the HaHaHouse began."
她在一天之內就想出了博物館許多元素的構想：「哈哈屋就是這樣開始的。」
Golubic said a picture of her when she was seven-year-old inspired her.
戈魯比奇說，一張她七歲時的照片給了她靈感。
“I was constantly joking as a kid," she added.
「我小時候總是一直在開玩笑。」她補充說。
Visitors press a button to be "disinfected from negativity" as soon as they step inside the museum, which has eight interactive zones, or areas.
遊客一進入博物館，就會按下按鈕來「消毒負面情緒」；館內共有八個互動區域。
One has rubber chickens singing cheerfully.
其中一區有開心唱歌的橡膠雞。
They sing songs like ABBA's "Dancing Queen.
牠們會唱ABBA合唱團的〈Dancing Queen〉等歌曲。
There is a karaoke room with distorted voices and a "Sumo Arena" for wrestling in puffed up clothes.
還有一間會讓聲音變調的卡拉OK室，以及一個穿著充氣衣服摔角的「相撲競技場」。
There is also some serious history of humor from ancient to modern times told through theatre, film or the internet.
館內也有一些嚴肅的幽默史，透過戲劇、電影或網路，介紹從古至今的幽默。
The museum also explains different kinds of humor.
博物館也解說了不同類型的幽默。
These include word play, slapstick, dark humor and satire.
包括文字遊戲、鬧劇、黑色幽默和諷刺。
Golubic said the HaHaHouse is popular with everyone from small children to older people.
戈魯比奇說，哈哈屋從小孩到長者都很喜歡。
Adults say it is a good excuse to act like a child.
大人們說，這是讓自己像個孩子一樣的好藉口。
"All those who still feel a bit of childish joy and embrace their inner child, will recharge themselves," she said.
「所有仍保有一點童心、擁抱內在小孩的人，都能在這裡為自己充電。」她說。
Retiree Bruno Dadic told AFP he was pleased by his visit "as there is never enough humor in life.
退休人士布魯諾．達迪奇（Bruno Dadic）告訴法新社，他對這次參觀很滿意，「因為人生中的幽默永遠不嫌多」。
"Laughter is a medicine for the soul," he said.
「笑是心靈的良藥。」他說。
Aleksandar Suka celebrated his fifth birthday with a visit.
亞歷山大．蘇卡（Aleksandar Suka）以參觀博物館來慶祝自己的五歲生日。
Visiting with his mother, the little boy said he liked lying on the "Bed of Nails" since they tickled him.
這個跟媽媽一起來的小男孩說，他喜歡躺在「釘床」上，因為那些釘子會搔他癢。
Singer Zorica Bucic, from the coastal town of Split, said the museum was just right for our times.
來自沿海城鎮斯普利特的歌手佐莉卡．布契奇（Zorica Bucic）說，這座博物館正適合我們這個時代。
"Entering here is like entering childhood, being relieved of all problems,” she said.
「走進這裡就像走進童年，所有問題都一掃而空。」她說。
Bucic added that if you could come to museum often, you would not need to visit a psychologist.
布契奇補充說，如果能常來這座博物館，就不需要去看心理師了。
Psychologist Petar Kraljevic told AFP that laughter is a kind of weapon which gives people strength to face their problems.
心理師佩塔．克拉列維奇（Petar Kraljevic）告訴法新社，笑是一種武器，能給人面對問題的力量。
He said that if doctors could advise their patients to have "three hours of laughter” a day, people would feel much better.
他說，如果醫生能建議病人每天「笑三小時」，大家會感覺好很多。

articles.title: The Paradox Museum Miami Aims to Trick the Eye
articles.titleZh: 邁阿密悖論博物館要騙過你的眼睛

s: Paradox Museum Miami is a mixture of art, science, and fun.
邁阿密悖論博物館（Paradox Museum Miami）融合了藝術、科學與樂趣。
The 1,000-square-meter museum is housed in Miami's Wynwood arts and entertainment area.
這座1000平方公尺的博物館位於邁阿密的溫伍德（Wynwood）藝術娛樂區。
It has more than 70 public displays known as exhibits.
館內有70多項公開展示，也就是展品。
Executive director Samantha Impellizeri says these exhibits challenge the imagination.
執行長莎曼珊．因佩利澤里（Samantha Impellizeri）說，這些展品挑戰人們的想像力。
She added that visitors can walk away from the experience with some really fun and interesting material for social media.
她補充說，遊客參觀完後，可以帶走一些非常有趣、好玩的社群媒體素材。
Paradox Museum has more than ten locations throughout North America, Europe and Asia.
悖論博物館在北美、歐洲和亞洲有十多個據點。
The Miami location, which opened in 2022, was the first in North America.
2022年開幕的邁阿密館是北美第一家。
The term paradox is central to the museum and what visitors experience.
「悖論」一詞是這座博物館及遊客體驗的核心。
A paradox is a situation or thing that has seemingly opposite or contradictory qualities.
悖論是指看似具有相反或矛盾特質的情況或事物。
“Each paradox is uniquely tied to its community,” Impellizeri said.
「每一座悖論博物館都與當地社區有獨特的連結。」因佩利澤里說。
“So as you walk throughout the experience, you’ll notice different themes and art installations that directly reflect not only Miami but the Wynwood community specifically."
「所以當你一路參觀時，會注意到不同的主題和藝術裝置，不只直接反映邁阿密，更特別反映溫伍德社區。」
Many of the displays at Paradox Museum suggest old carnival funhouses – buildings that had devices and rooms designed to surprise or amaze visitors.
悖論博物館的許多展示讓人聯想到以前嘉年華會的遊樂屋——那些設有各種裝置和房間、專門讓遊客驚喜或驚嘆的建築。
Examples include the mirror maze, the spinning tunnel, and the upside-down room.
例如鏡子迷宮、旋轉隧道和顛倒屋。
The difference is that Paradox Museum explains the math and science behind each illusion.
不同的是，悖論博物館會解說每種錯覺背後的數學和科學原理。
“We’re a top field trip destination for pre-K all the way up through college students,” Impellizeri said.
「從幼兒園到大學生，我們都是首選的校外教學地點。」因佩利澤里說。
She added that the museum has a large number of educational activities that students can do before, during, and after the visit.
她補充說，博物館有大量教育活動，學生在參觀前、參觀中和參觀後都可以進行。
Like any museum, Paradox Museum plans to change its exhibits to keep visitors coming back.
和其他博物館一樣，悖論博物館也計畫更換展品，讓遊客一再回訪。
“We’re not going to be the same space in a year to three years from now," Impellizeri said.
「一年到三年後，我們不會是同一個樣子。」因佩利澤里說。
Paradox Museum Miami introduced a new Zero Gravity Room last fall.
邁阿密悖論博物館去年秋天推出了新的「無重力室」。
Visitors can turn their smart phone cameras on and attach their phones to a spinning holder.
遊客可以打開智慧型手機的相機，把手機固定在一個旋轉支架上。
Then they step into a large, slowly moving room designed to look like the inside of a space station.
接著，他們走進一個設計成太空站內部模樣、緩慢轉動的大房間。
The resulting video makes it look as though they are walking up the wall and ceiling inside a room unaffected by gravity.
拍出來的影片看起來就像他們在不受重力影響的房間裡，沿著牆壁和天花板走路。
Paradox Museum is part of a movement towards so-called “immersive art experiences.
悖論博物館是所謂「沉浸式藝術體驗」風潮的一部分。
These kinds of art experiences often use technology to make the visitors feel like they are taking part in art rather than just looking at it.
這類藝術體驗常運用科技，讓遊客覺得自己是在參與藝術，而不只是觀看。
“Immersive experiences around the world are increasing in popularity,” Impellizeri noted.
「沉浸式體驗在全世界越來越受歡迎。」因佩利澤里指出。
Immersive art experiences have opened all over the world during the past 10 years or so.
過去十年左右，世界各地紛紛出現沉浸式藝術體驗。

Examples include a company called Meow Wolf with several locations in the western United States, as well as a Van Gogh exhibit that has been traveling through North America, Europe and Asia since 2017.
例子包括在美國西部有多個據點的Meow Wolf公司，以及自2017年起在北美、歐洲和亞洲巡迴展出的梵谷展。
Superblue Miami, which opened in 2021, is another example.
2021年開幕的Superblue邁阿密也是一例。
Visitors generally take 60 to 90 minutes to make their way through Paradox Museum.
遊客參觀悖論博物館一般需要60到90分鐘。
Tickets normally cost $26 for adults and teenagers and $20 for children.
門票通常成人及青少年26美元，兒童20美元。
Seventeen-year-old Facundo Ildarraz and his family came to Miami from Argentina.
17歲的法昆多．伊爾達拉斯（Facundo Ildarraz）和家人從阿根廷來到邁阿密。
Ildarraz said his mother found Paradox Museum online.
伊爾達拉斯說，他媽媽是在網路上找到悖論博物館的。
He said it turned out to be a great chance to take fun photos with his family.
他說，結果這是和家人拍有趣照片的大好機會。
“I’ve been laughing since I went inside,” Ildarraz said.
「我從進來到現在一直在笑。」伊爾達拉斯說。
“It’s really amazing.”
「真的太神奇了。」
Dennis Speigel is head of a business advisory company called International Theme Park Services, Inc. Speigel said immersive experiences are a natural progression of location-based entertainment.
丹尼斯．史匹格（Dennis Speigel）是商業顧問公司「國際主題樂園服務公司」的負責人，史匹格說，沉浸式體驗是定點娛樂的自然演進。
Location-based entertainment includes go-cart tracks, laser tag, paint ball, indoor skydiving, escape rooms and trampoline parks.
定點娛樂包括卡丁車場、雷射槍對戰、漆彈、室內跳傘、密室逃脫和彈跳床樂園。
These are activities that take visitors a few hours to go through.
這些都是遊客要花幾個小時才能玩完的活動。
“It’s a lot of little things that we’ve had in the industry for years, heightened by our new technology…to make the experience new and something people haven’t seen,” Speigel said.
「這些是業界多年來就有的許多小東西，再透過我們的新科技加以強化……讓體驗變得新穎，是人們從沒見過的。」史匹格說。

articles.title: What is the Super Bowl?
articles.titleZh: 超級盃是什麼？

s: This Sunday, February 9, is not a holiday in the United States, but it might seem like one to Americans.
這個星期日，2月9日，在美國並不是假日，但對美國人來說可能像是過節一樣。
Many will be attending parties to watch Super Bowl LIX.
許多人會參加派對收看第59屆超級盃（Super Bowl LIX）。
The Super Bowl is the championship game of professional American football.
超級盃是美國職業美式足球的冠軍賽。
The National Football League, or NFL, has 32 teams mainly based in large cities across the U.S.
國家美式足球聯盟（NFL）有32支球隊，主要設在美國各大城市。
The first professional league was formed in 1920, when representatives of four teams met in Canton, Ohio.
第一個職業聯盟成立於1920年，當時四支球隊的代表在俄亥俄州坎頓市開會。
The group first called itself the American Professional Football Association but changed the name two years later to the National Football League.
這個團體最初自稱「美國職業美式足球協會」，兩年後改名為「國家美式足球聯盟」。
In 1960, Texas businessman Lamar Hunt pushed the effort to create the American Football League, or AFL.
1960年，德州商人拉馬爾．杭特（Lamar Hunt）推動成立了美國美式足球聯盟（AFL）。
The two leagues competed with each other to sign top football players from universities around the country.
兩個聯盟互相競爭，爭取簽下全國各大學的頂尖球員。
In 1965, established NFL players began negotiating to play for the competing league.
1965年，NFL的知名球員開始洽談轉戰對手聯盟。
So, officials of the two leagues decided to work together.
於是兩個聯盟的高層決定合作。
This agreement established a championship game between the two leagues.
這項協議促成了兩個聯盟之間的冠軍賽。
It was officially called the AFL-NFL World Championship Game but became known as the Super Bowl.
它的正式名稱是「AFL－NFL世界冠軍賽」，但後來被稱為超級盃。
The first Super Bowl was played in 1967 in Los Angeles, California.
第一屆超級盃於1967年在加州洛杉磯舉行。
The Green Bay Packers defeated the Kansas City Chiefs.
綠灣包裝工隊擊敗了堪薩斯城酋長隊。
It was not a very exciting game.
那場比賽並不怎麼精彩。
Many of the seats in the sports center were empty.
體育場裡許多座位都是空的。
That changed with the Super Bowl played two years later.
兩年後的超級盃改變了這一切。
Experts say the public finally accepted the new league when the New York Jets defeated the Baltimore Colts.
專家說，當紐約噴射機隊擊敗巴爾的摩小馬隊時，大眾終於接受了這個新聯盟。
After that game in 1969, officials of the two leagues decided to create a new National Football League.
1969年那場比賽後，兩個聯盟的高層決定成立新的國家美式足球聯盟。
They divided the teams into two competing conferences, the American Conference, or AFC, and the National Conference, NFC.
他們把球隊分成兩個互相競爭的聯會：美國聯會（AFC）和國家聯會（NFC）。
Each year, the conference champions play in the Super Bowl.
每年兩個聯會的冠軍會在超級盃對決。
Today, the Super Bowl is a major sporting event.
如今，超級盃是一項重大的體育賽事。
Tens of thousands of people will be watching the game Sunday at the Superdome in New Orleans, Louisiana.
星期日將有數萬人在路易斯安那州紐奧良的超級巨蛋觀賽。
Tens of millions of other people around the world will be watching Super Bowl LIX.
全球還有數千萬人會收看第59屆超級盃。
They will be watching to see if the AFC Kansas City Chiefs or the NFC Philadelphia Eagles become the champions of American football.
他們要看看是AFC的堪薩斯城酋長隊，還是NFC的費城老鷹隊，會成為美式足球的冠軍。
Both teams have had success in the Big Game.
兩支球隊在這場「大賽」中都曾有佳績。
The Eagles are one-time NFL champions.
老鷹隊曾拿過一次NFL冠軍。
They defeated the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LII.
他們在第52屆超級盃擊敗了新英格蘭愛國者隊。
This Sunday will be the team’s fifth NFL championship game appearance.
這個星期日將是該隊第五次打進NFL冠軍賽。
The Kansas City Chiefs have played for the championship six times.
堪薩斯城酋長隊曾六度爭奪冠軍。
They have won four times, including the last two Super Bowls.
他們贏了四次，包括最近兩屆超級盃。
The Chiefs are the first team in NFL history to have a chance to win a third Super Bowl in a row.
酋長隊是NFL史上第一支有機會拿下超級盃三連霸的球隊。

articles.title: What is the Best Kind of Yoga for Beginners?
articles.titleZh: 初學者最適合哪種瑜伽？

s: The activity called yoga means different things to different people around the world.
瑜伽這項活動，對世界各地不同的人有不同的意義。
The word itself comes from the Sanskrit language and means “union.”
這個字本身源自梵文，意思是「結合」。
For some, yoga is an exercise centered on mindful breathing and slow movement.
對有些人來說，瑜伽是一種以正念呼吸和緩慢動作為核心的運動。
For others, it is a series of difficult body movements and positioning designed to improve health and fitness.
對另一些人來說，它是一系列困難的身體動作和姿勢，目的是增進健康和體能。
Still others consider yoga a spiritual exercise.
還有些人認為瑜伽是一種心靈修練。
And there are many people for whom yoga is a combination of all or some of these things.
也有許多人認為瑜伽是上述全部或部分元素的結合。
So, yoga takes many different forms around the world.
因此，瑜伽在世界各地有許多不同的形式。
All kinds of yoga involve positions known as poses (asanas).
所有瑜伽都包含稱為「體位法」（asanas）的姿勢。
But the positions and training can differ even under yoga methods, or styles, of the same name, including hatha, vinyasa, Iyengar and others.
但即使是同名的瑜伽方法或流派，例如哈達、流動（vinyasa）、艾揚格等，姿勢和訓練方式也可能不同。
So, what is the best kind of yoga training for a beginner?
那麼，初學者最適合哪種瑜伽訓練呢？
“The best is the one that works for you,” said Tim Senesi, who has been teaching yoga in Orange County, California, for 22 years.
「最好的就是適合你的那一種。」在加州橘郡教瑜伽22年的提姆．塞內西（Tim Senesi）說。
“There are many different paths leading toward the same aim,” he added.
「有許多不同的道路通往同一個目標。」他補充說。
Hatha, meaning “force,” describes any kind of yoga class involving asanas.
哈達的意思是「力量」，泛指任何包含體位法的瑜伽課。
A sun salutation, for example, is an important series of 12 asanas that begin many kinds of yoga classes.
例如拜日式就是一套重要的12個體位法，許多瑜伽課都以它開場。
Training under the hatha name, however, is usually gentler than others and more centered on breathing exercises, called pranayama.
不過，以哈達為名的訓練通常比其他流派溫和，也更著重呼吸練習，也就是「調息法」（pranayama）。
Poses are held for a few breaths and students usually move more slowly.
每個姿勢會維持幾次呼吸，學員的動作通常也比較慢。
Hatha can be good for beginners who are looking to relax while improving flexibility and balance.
想要放鬆、同時提升柔軟度和平衡感的初學者，很適合哈達瑜伽。
Another style, yin, pays even more attention to recovery by working to stretch the muscles’ connective tissue.
另一個流派「陰瑜伽」更重視恢復，著重伸展肌肉的結締組織。
Students hold poses for 5 minutes or more, permitting the body to settle into a pose rather than pushing it.
學員每個姿勢要維持5分鐘以上，讓身體慢慢沉入姿勢，而不是硬撐。
A more difficult, flowing form of yoga is known as vinyasa.
一種難度較高、動作連貫的瑜伽稱為流動瑜伽（vinyasa）。
It mixes movement with breath over a series of asanas.
它在一系列體位法中結合動作與呼吸。
Some higher-level vinyasa classes move at a rate of one movement per breath.
有些較高階的流動瑜伽課，速度是一個呼吸一個動作。
In the United States, these classes are often called Flow or Power yoga.
在美國，這類課程常被稱為「流動瑜伽」或「力量瑜伽」。
They can be good for people who are more athletic.
它們很適合運動能力較好的人。
Still, teachers suggest that even athletic students start with a beginner level.
不過，老師們建議即使是運動型的學員，也要從初級開始。

“I wouldn’t really encourage them to start in a higher level vinyasa flow class because they’re not going to have the foundation to move safely through that,” said Anne Van Valkenburg, of Lanai, Hawaii.
「我不太會鼓勵他們一開始就上高階的流動瑜伽課，因為他們還沒有足夠的基礎可以安全地完成動作。」夏威夷拉奈島的安．范瓦肯堡（Anne Van Valkenburg）說。
She has been training yoga teachers in a mix of methods for 18 years.
她以多種方法混合的方式培訓瑜伽老師已有18年。
Ashtanga yoga is similar to vinyasa.
阿斯坦加瑜伽和流動瑜伽很類似。
However, ashtanga involves a set series of poses that students repeat day after day, often going at their own speed.
不過，阿斯坦加有一套固定的姿勢序列，學員日復一日重複練習，通常按照自己的速度進行。
As students get stronger and more skilled, they move up to a higher series with more difficult poses.
隨著學員變得更強壯、更熟練，就會晉升到姿勢更難的高階序列。
Iyengar style involves the same poses as vinyasa, but classes usually move at a slower pace.
艾揚格瑜伽的姿勢和流動瑜伽相同，但課程節奏通常比較慢。
However, the poses are not necessarily easier.
不過，這些姿勢不一定比較簡單。
Iyengar yoga pays special attention to carefully moving or aligning parts of the body.
艾揚格瑜伽特別注重身體各部位的細心移動與對齊。
Poses are held for longer and students often use supportive equipment during the exercise.
姿勢維持的時間較長，學員在練習時也常使用輔助器材。
Iyengar is especially good for people recovering from injuries.
艾揚格瑜伽特別適合正在從受傷中復原的人。
It can also be a good fit for physically active people who want to get the basics of yoga before moving into different styles.
對於想先打好瑜伽基礎、再嘗試其他流派的活躍人士來說，它也很合適。
These days, teachers often mix different yoga methods in a single class.
現在，老師們常在一堂課中混合不同的瑜伽方法。
And many classes are not named under any traditional method.
而且許多課程並沒有冠上任何傳統流派的名稱。
The AP suggests that if you are interested in starting to practice yoga, you should look for a beginner series.
美聯社建議，如果你有興趣開始練瑜伽，應該找初學者系列課程。
But if you cannot find one that is right, do not worry.
但如果找不到合適的，也不用擔心。
Most teachers are happy to have beginners in their classes and will alter the training to meet the needs of students new to yoga.
大多數老師都很歡迎初學者來上課，並會調整訓練內容，以符合瑜伽新手的需求。
Most of all, try a few classes until you find the method or teacher who is a good fit for you.
最重要的是，多試幾堂課，直到找到適合你的方法或老師。
“I feel sad when someone tries yoga once or twice and they’re like, ‘Eh, I don’t like it,’” Van Valkenburg said, adding, “there’s just so much out there that you might be missing...”
「看到有人試了一兩次瑜伽就說『呃，我不喜歡』，我會覺得很可惜。」范瓦肯堡說，她還補充：「外面還有好多東西，你可能就這樣錯過了……」

articles.title: Using Real Trees to Bring Nature Indoors
articles.titleZh: 用真樹把大自然帶進室內

s: There is a growing movement worldwide to use plants in building design to establish closer connections with nature and soften hard city styles.
在建築設計中運用植物，以拉近與大自然的距離、柔化冷硬的城市風格，正成為一股日漸興起的全球風潮。
The movement also seeks to improve designs to help protect the environment and increase personal wellness.
這股風潮也希望改善設計，以幫助保護環境並增進個人健康。
Many of the efforts by architects and designers have centered on one natural element: trees.
建築師和設計師的許多努力，都聚焦在一種自然元素上：樹木。
Examples of such design can be found in many places, including New York City.
這類設計的例子在許多地方都看得到，包括紐約市。
A building in Manhattan that houses the Ford Foundation has a 12-story light-filled entrance area, or atrium.
曼哈頓一棟福特基金會所在的大樓，有一個12層樓高、光線充足的入口區域，也就是中庭。
It is also filled with plants and flowers including magnolias, eucalyptus, jacaranda, cryptomeria, iron bark and pear trees.
那裡也種滿了植物和花卉，包括木蘭、尤加利、藍花楹、柳杉、鐵皮桉和梨樹。
Another example sits within New York City’s Brookfield Place shopping center.
另一個例子位於紐約市的布魯克菲爾德廣場購物中心。
The center’s main atrium includes a collection of 12-meter-tall Washingtonia palm trees.
該中心的主中庭有一整排12公尺高的華盛頓棕櫚樹。
In Singapore, the city-state’s Jewel Changi airport offers travelers an inviting environment.
在新加坡，這個城市國家的星耀樟宜機場為旅客提供了一個宜人的環境。
It has 2,500 trees native to nations including Madagascar, Australia, Malaysia and Indonesia.
那裡有2500棵原產於馬達加斯加、澳洲、馬來西亞和印尼等國的樹木。
The airport includes a 2.4-hectare indoor forest with walking paths.
機場內有一座2.4公頃、設有步道的室內森林。
Some apartments and mixed-use buildings are also putting trees and other greenery into their designs.
一些公寓和複合式建築也把樹木和其他綠色植物融入設計中。
Such buildings are sometimes called “greenscrapers,” a term that comes from the word “skyscraper.”
這類建築有時被稱為「綠色摩天樓」（greenscraper），這個詞源自「摩天大樓」（skyscraper）。
In Milan, Italy, architect Stefano Boeri designed Bosco Verticale, a 44-story building with 800 trees and other greenery.
在義大利米蘭，建築師斯特凡諾．博埃里（Stefano Boeri）設計了「垂直森林」（Bosco Verticale），這是一棟有800棵樹和其他綠色植物的44層大樓。
In the Netherlands, he also built the Trudo Vertical Forest.
他也在荷蘭建造了「特魯多垂直森林」（Trudo Vertical Forest）。
This is a low-income apartment building with trees growing on all sides.
這是一棟四面都長著樹的低收入戶公寓大樓。
Similar changes are also happening inside private homes.
類似的變化也發生在私人住宅裡。
In some, trees are brought right indoors.
有些住宅直接把樹搬進室內。
In others, outdoor trees are carefully placed as important partners in the building plan.
另一些則精心安排戶外樹木的位置，讓它們成為建築規劃中的重要夥伴。
Some architects even build homes around existing trees.
有些建築師甚至圍繞著原有的樹木蓋房子。
Others plant one or more trees inside the home.
也有人在屋內種一棵或多棵樹。
And some architects or designers imagine natural settings indoors by using parts of trees.
還有些建築師或設計師利用樹木的部分材料，在室內營造自然場景。
These designs are meant to create the look and feel of real wood, while bringing feelings of peace and calm.
這些設計旨在營造真實木材的外觀和質感，同時帶來平靜祥和的感受。

paras.h: A calm heart of the home

s: Ryoko Okada is an architect at New York City’s Oda Architecture.
岡田涼子（Ryoko Okada）是紐約市Oda建築事務所的建築師。
She told The Associated Press that she and her co-workers aim to bring outdoor elements indoors as often as they can.
她告訴美聯社，她和同事們的目標是盡可能把戶外元素帶進室內。
“There’s nothing more calming than being surrounded by nature…” Okada said.
「沒有什麼比被大自然環繞更讓人平靜的了……」岡田說。
She added that a living tree indoors can bring peace and happiness as people watch it grow and change.
她補充說，室內的活樹能讓人們在看著它生長變化時，感到平靜和快樂。

paras.h: Framing the views with existing trees

s: Another design example came from KAA Design Group in Los Angeles.
另一個設計案例來自洛杉磯的KAA設計集團。
A team from the company created a modern home that uses the property’s existing trees, such as cork oaks, rare Torrey pines, and magnolias.
該公司的團隊打造了一棟現代住宅，運用了基地上原有的樹木，例如栓皮櫟、稀有的托里松和木蘭。
One very large, old cork oak sits in the center of the property.
一棵非常巨大的老栓皮櫟就位於基地中央。
At first, the owners did not like the look and said they wanted the tree gone.
起初，屋主不喜歡它的樣子，說想把這棵樹移走。
One of the company’s partners, Grant Kirkpatrick, had to persuade the homeowners to keep it.
該公司的合夥人之一葛蘭特．柯克派翠克（Grant Kirkpatrick）必須說服屋主留下它。
Kirkpatrick explained he succeeded by pointing out that the tree was “a 300-year-old antique that should be featured rather than removed.”
柯克派翠克解釋說，他成功的方法是指出這棵樹是「一件300年的古董，應該加以展現，而不是移除」。
The driveway on that property also offers a calming design.
那棟房子的車道也有讓人放鬆的設計。
A black pine tree rises up from the driveway like a piece of natural art.
一棵黑松從車道上拔地而起，就像一件天然藝術品。
In addition, views from almost every window in the house feature the beautiful nature outdoors.
此外，從屋內幾乎每扇窗戶望出去，都能看到戶外美麗的自然景色。
Okada says she suggests people do not plant a full-size tree in their home without first seeking expert advice.
岡田說，她建議人們不要在沒有先尋求專家意見的情況下，在家裡種一棵完整大小的樹。
She notes that a living tree will only do well if certain conditions – such as air, light and soil – are right.
她指出，活樹只有在空氣、光線和土壤等特定條件都合適時，才能長得好。
Okada added that a living tree “…needs to be supported by proper infrastructure to stay alive and avoid home damage.
岡田補充說，活樹「……需要適當的基礎設施支撐，才能存活並避免損壞房屋。」
She also urges people to heavily research a tree’s natural environment to avoid drawing in unwanted pests.
她也呼籲人們要好好研究樹木的自然生長環境，以免引來不速之客般的害蟲。
Kirkpatrick noted that planting a tree indoors can be difficult.
柯克派翠克指出，在室內種樹可能很困難。
He explained that at least 1.2 meters of soil depth is needed, along with lots of natural light and the right temperature.
他解釋說，至少需要1.2公尺深的土壤，還要有充足的自然光和合適的溫度。

paras.h: Other ways to use trees besides having a live one
paras.hz: 除了種活樹以外，其他運用樹木的方式

s: Kirkpatrick said he worked on one property that experienced a serious fire in 2016.
柯克派翠克說，他曾參與一處在2016年遭遇嚴重火災的房產。
His team decided to use parts from one of the burned manzanita trees in the interior design.
他的團隊決定把一棵燒焦的熊果樹（manzanita）的部分枝幹用在室內設計中。
The piece was painted black and placed inside the property.
這件作品被漆成黑色，擺放在房子裡。
He said it now represents an eye-catching, natural art piece.
他說，現在它是一件吸睛的天然藝術品。

articles.title: Researchers Uncover a Bathhouse Complex in Ancient Pompeii
articles.titleZh: 研究人員在古城龐貝發現浴場建築群

s: Archeological research has uncovered another treasure of the ancient Roman city of Pompeii: a large private bathhouse.
考古研究在古羅馬城市龐貝又發現了一項寶藏：一座大型私人浴場。
The explosion of Mount Vesuvius in 70 AD buried Pompeii in thick ash, wreckage, and lava, or hot liquid rock.
西元70年維蘇威火山爆發，用厚厚的火山灰、殘骸和熔岩（也就是高溫的液態岩石）掩埋了龐貝城。
Archeologists are continuing to find remains of the city under the ground.
考古學家仍持續在地底下發現這座城市的遺跡。
The bathhouse was part of a large private house, the scientists said.
科學家說，這座浴場是一棟大型私人宅邸的一部分。
The bathhouse holds a series of rooms that would have provided hot, warm, or cold conditions.
浴場有一系列房間，分別提供熱、溫或冷的環境。
The art and design of the complex, including mosaic works, also suggest the owner was wealthy.
這個建築群的藝術與設計，包括馬賽克作品，也顯示屋主相當富有。
“We have here perhaps the largest thermal complex in a private house in Pompeii,” said Gabriel Zuchtriegel, director of the Pompeii Archaeological Park.
「這裡可能是龐貝私人住宅中規模最大的溫泉浴場建築群。」龐貝考古園區主任加布里埃爾．祖赫特里格爾（Gabriel Zuchtriegel）說。
He explained that Pompeii’s powerful and wealthy set up large spaces at their homes to hold major gatherings for ceremonies and other purposes.
他解釋說，龐貝的權貴和富人會在家中設置大型空間，用來舉辦典禮等各種大型聚會。
“It was an opportunity to show the wealth in which they lived and also to have a nice thermal treatment," he said.
「這是展現他們富裕生活的機會，同時也能享受舒服的溫泉療程。」他說。
The baths were unearthed in the so-called Regio IX, a large central area of Pompeii Park that is still unexplored.
這座浴場是在所謂的「第九區」（Regio IX）出土的，那是龐貝園區中央一大片仍未探勘的區域。
Recently, archeologists working in the same area found a bakery, a laundry and two homes.
最近，考古學家在同一區域發現了一間麵包店、一間洗衣坊和兩棟住宅。
They also found the bones of three people who died in the volcanic burst.
他們也發現了三名死於火山爆發者的骨骸。
Pompeii was not the only city destroyed in the explosion.
龐貝並不是唯一在這次爆發中被摧毀的城市。
It also buried the city of Herculaneum.
它也掩埋了赫庫蘭尼姆城。
Zuchtriegel said wealthy citizens of Pompeii often would first take a bath and then attend a banquet, or a big meal.
祖赫特里格爾說，龐貝的富裕市民常會先洗澡，再去參加宴會，也就是一頓大餐。
The private thermal complex permitted them to do so together at the home where the banquet was held.
私人溫泉浴場讓他們能在舉辦宴會的宅邸裡一起完成這些事。
“There is room for about 30 people who could do the whole routine, and that could also be done in public baths.
「這裡大約可容納30人完成整套流程，而這些流程在公共浴場也可以做。
So there is the caldarium, a very warm environment, and also a large tub with cold water,” he said.
所以這裡有熱水浴室（caldarium），一個非常溫暖的環境，還有一個裝冷水的大浴池。」他說。

articles.title: What Is Art Deco and Why Is It Popular Again?
articles.titleZh: 什麼是裝飾藝術？為何再度流行？

s: Art Deco is an international artistic style that was popular in the 1920s and 1930s.
裝飾藝術（Art Deco）是1920和1930年代流行的國際藝術風格。
Now, interest in the style and its qualities is growing.
如今，人們對這種風格及其特色的興趣日益增加。
A new generation is enjoying the style’s roots and turning it into something new.
新世代喜愛這種風格的根源，並將它轉化為新的事物。
A public showing, or exhibition, at the Museum of the City of New York provides a look at the style that helped define the city 100 years ago.
紐約市立博物館的一場公開展覽，讓人一窺這種在100年前幫助定義紐約的風格。
Famous Art Deco buildings include the Chrysler Building, the Empire State Building, Rockefeller Center and Radio City Music Hall.
著名的裝飾藝術建築包括克萊斯勒大樓、帝國大廈、洛克斐勒中心和無線電城音樂廳。
The public showing, called “Art Deco City: New York Postcards from the Leonard A. Lauder Collection,” also has clothing and film clips from the time.
這場名為「裝飾藝術之城：李奧納德．A．勞德收藏的紐約明信片」的展覽，也展出了當時的服飾和電影片段。
In London, the Victoria and Albert Museum has a collection of day and evening clothing, jewelry and more.
在倫敦，維多利亞與亞伯特博物館收藏了日間和晚間服飾、珠寶等。
The collection comes from Les Ballets Russes, a dance company that had a major effect on fashion.
這些收藏來自對時尚有重大影響的舞團「俄羅斯芭蕾舞團」（Les Ballets Russes）。
And in Paris, organizers of the 2024 Olympics created Art Deco posters last year to celebrate the games and mark the one hundred years since the 1924 Olympics, which Paris also hosted.
而在巴黎，2024年奧運的籌辦單位去年製作了裝飾藝術風格的海報，以慶祝奧運，並紀念同樣由巴黎主辦的1924年奧運屆滿一百年。
Experts have different opinions about Art Deco.
專家們對裝飾藝術有不同的看法。
Design writer Arricca Elin Sansone, for example, said last year in Elle Décor magazine: “Ask three historians to define the term Art Deco, and you’ll likely get three varying answers.”
例如，設計作家阿麗卡．艾琳．桑索恩（Arricca Elin Sansone）去年在《Elle Décor》雜誌中寫道：「請三位歷史學家定義『裝飾藝術』，你很可能會得到三種不同的答案。」
Appearing after World War I, the first Art Deco era had a spirit of creativity and freedom.
裝飾藝術出現於第一次世界大戰後，最初的時代充滿創意與自由的精神。
With the aim of appearing modern, the style became one of the most important forms of design in the 1920s and early 1930s.
這種風格以展現現代感為目標，成為1920年代和1930年代初期最重要的設計形式之一。
The Art Deco style is believed to have first appeared at the 1925 International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts, in Paris.
一般認為，裝飾藝術風格最早出現在1925年於巴黎舉行的「國際現代裝飾與工業藝術博覽會」。
The early 1930s saw the development of the style in Miami where South Beach’s Art Deco District is popular with visitors and a center for design.
1930年代初期，這種風格在邁阿密發展，當地南灘的裝飾藝術區很受遊客歡迎，也是設計重鎮。
In some large cities, low-rise buildings of two or three floors turned into landscapes of high-rise skyscrapers.
在一些大城市，兩三層樓的低矮建築變成了高聳摩天大樓林立的景觀。
Public and private spaces showed themes involving geometrical designs and luxurious materials.
公共和私人空間都呈現出幾何設計和奢華材質的主題。
In transportation, faster cars and better trains suggested a new age while jazz music urged people to celebrate.
在交通方面，更快的汽車和更好的火車預示著新時代的來臨，而爵士樂則鼓舞人們歡慶。
The same energy can be found in today’s fashion shows and red-carpet events for stars.
同樣的活力也能在今天的時裝秀和明星紅毯活動中看到。
Some of today’s colorful clothing suggests the Jazz Age, another name for the period when Art Deco was popular.
現今一些色彩繽紛的服裝讓人聯想到「爵士時代」，也就是裝飾藝術流行時期的另一個名稱。
Stars like Zendaya, Gigi Hadid, Beyoncé and Demi Lovato have used elements of the Deco era in new ways.
千黛亞（Zendaya）、吉吉．哈蒂德、碧昂絲和黛咪．洛瓦特等明星，都以新的方式運用了裝飾藝術時代的元素。
“The aesthetic of the 1920s is enjoying a fashionable renaissance,” said Kirsty Thatcher of the Australian fashion magazine Russh.
「1920年代的美學正迎來一場時尚的文藝復興。」澳洲時尚雜誌《Russh》的克絲蒂．柴契爾（Kirsty Thatcher）說。
A “renaissance” represents a rebirth of something from the past.
「文藝復興」代表過去某樣事物的重生。
New York-based interior designer Vanessa DeLeon told the Associated Press, “The boldness and elegance of Art Deco are what appeals to me.”
紐約室內設計師凡妮莎．德里昂（Vanessa DeLeon）告訴美聯社：「裝飾藝術的大膽與優雅，正是吸引我的地方。」
Jamie Watkins and Tom Kennedy of the London design company Divine Savages include Art Deco elements in their collections of products for the home.
倫敦設計公司Divine Savages的潔米．華金斯（Jamie Watkins）和湯姆．甘迺迪（Tom Kennedy），在他們的居家產品系列中加入了裝飾藝術元素。
Watkins suggested: “It’s no wonder we’re drawn to it again.”
華金斯表示：「難怪我們會再次被它吸引。」
Lynda Klich is the co-organizer or curator of the exhibition at the Museum of the City of New York.
琳達．克里奇（Lynda Klich）是紐約市立博物館這場展覽的共同策展人。
Klich noted that postcards were the social media of their day.
克里奇指出，明信片就是當時的社群媒體。
Travelers at the time busily wrote messages to friends and family.
當時的旅人忙著寫信息給親朋好友。
New York’s famous Art Deco buildings appear in over 250 postcards.
紐約著名的裝飾藝術建築出現在250多張明信片上。
There is also a selection of clothing from the 1920s, shoes and other objects.
展覽也精選了1920年代的服飾、鞋子和其他物品。
“Art Deco was the look that sold the city to the world,” said co-curator Lilly Tuttle.
「裝飾藝術就是把紐約推銷給全世界的那種風貌。」共同策展人莉莉．塔特爾（Lilly Tuttle）說。
The exhibition in New York City runs through February 17.
紐約市的這場展覽將展出到2月17日。
